The accommodation is centred around a welcoming reception hall with oak finished flooring and provides four good reception rooms which add to the flexibility of the living space on offer. Lawned gardens surround the house and there is a charming orchard area planted with numerous fruit trees to the Eastern side. Alongside the living kitchen and principal reception room is a very generous terraced area forming a lovely, sheltered seating area - an ideal spot for Al Fresco dining! Ilkley is blessed with a highly regarded schooling system, although a number of private schools for children of all ages are within easy access. Ilkley is surrounded by some of the finest countryside in the region - the river Wharfe and rugged moors offering many an opportunity for rural pursuits including stunning walks, challenging mountain biking and road cycling. text_description: It's not everyday that a house such as this one comes to the market in Honley. Situated off Hall Ing Lane, with local scenic walks on the doorstep, this three bedroom house has been improved by the present owners and offers superbly presented accommodation that makes the most of the character features, and blends them beautifully with modern comforts. The layout is a little unconventional and is best understood form our floorplans and 3D virtual tour. It's a home to fall in love with. On the ground floor is a beautiful modern fitted kitchen, complete with an integrated dishwasher, microwave, fridge, freezer and cooker hood (cooker by negotiation), with lovely fitted units and white quartz worktops. Further complemented by beautiful stone flagged flooring and an Inglenook fireplace with an inset wood burning stove. There is a very useful utility room and an adjacent recently installed contemporary shower room. An eye catching dining room with an exposed vaulted ceiling completes the ground floor, and stairs with recessed shelving rise to the first floor. The first floor is also at ground level with a useful porch and pedestrian access at the rear of the house (our ground floor could be described as lower ground floor). The lounge is very spacious and has a Juliet balcony from which to look out over the local area, and there is a focal point fireplace with an inset gas fired stove. There are feature beams and a lovely olde worlde entrance door. The bathroom which is just sumptuous, has a roll top bath and matching white basin and w.c. With well chosen tiling and flooring. Bedroom 3 is also on this level and is presently used as a an occasional bedroom with exercise bike (not included) - would make a good study too. On the top floor are two bedrooms and a landing. The main bedroom commands a lovely view, has a feature fireplace and some attractive fitted wardrobes as depicted in our images. The house is decorated in a most appealing neutral style with attractive floorings which complement the feel and style of this delightful house. In addition, there is a gas central heating system and double glazing. Externally, the property has a driveway providing parking and there is also a lawned garden with borders and seating area suited to alfresco dining etc. An early viewing is highly recommended to appreciate the property on offer. Honley is a much sought after semi rural and vibrant village in the Holme Valley, with something for everyone. Those who enjoy the outdoors will appreciate the local walks and scenery. There are sports and social clubs galore, a fabulous array of local amenities, independent shops, business and places to eat out and socialise. There are schools for children of all ages, making this an excellent location for families, and in addition, business travellers will appreciate the road and rail links to towns and cities further afield. The essentials: Mains services are available. The property is Freehold. Council Tax band D.

Downstairs, there are two vast reception rooms and a living area off the kitchen, making this a strong contender for the best house in North Leeds. This is a house of two halves: Where old meets new and the juxtaposition of the two styles sit unbelievably well together The kitchen space is of fine quality and all of the integral appliances are Miele: A built-in coffee machine, double ovens, microwave, two gas hobs, two induction hobs, an electric grill all with a dual vented extractor above - a hot plate, a dishwasher and a fridge freezer. Bi-folding doors divide this space, if required, into a beautiful living area where you can cosy up with a good book or film after a long day at work. text_description: Any family looking for a good sized home would be hard pressed to find something quite like this unique detached property. The style and design are simply one of a kind, and the accommodation is quite surprising. In any home, families are looking for good sized bedrooms, but here there are five doubles, and there are four full bathrooms to go with them, including three en-suite. But let's start with the ground floor. The entrance porch offers a great place for coats and shoes, but also screens the main living room from outside, meaning it keeps the room cooler in summer and warmer in winter. The main living room is quite a size, offering plenty of space for lounge and dining areas, and if this was the only room on this floor it would be a good size, however there's also a good sized sitting room, a large family dining kitchen, a big utility room and a cloakroom to this floor. The kitchen is the real hub of the house, and we can imagine spending plenty of time in here, the French doors open to the rear patio and gardens, and you certainly get that family gatherings feel in here. The utility has a door into the garage, which completes the ground floor. The main feature of the first floor is the principle bedroom suite which has a balcony looking across the fields to the moors off in the distance, as well as a large en-suite with a shaped bath, a walk in shower... All in all this really must be seen to be appreciated. EPC Rating: D Location The property is situated towards the top of Fleet Lane, across from the open fields. It's within a mile of the main shops and amenities in Queensbury, including the main Tesco, Russell Hall Primary School, Trinity Academy, etc. Postcode: BD13 2JL. Entrance Porch A good entrance which is a great way to screen the main living accommodation from the outside, particularly useful in more extreme weather temperatures to keep the indoor cooler in summer and warmer in winter. It’s also a great place for coats and shoes etc. Living Room (7.9m x 7.0m) A really good sized family room which narrows to 4.10 metres, and which has plenty of space for both lounge and dining areas, despite the amount of room for these facilities elsewhere in the house, and it offers so many possibilities for how you might use each room. There is a wood burning stove to one wall. Sitting Room (4.3m x 3.8m) By most homes' standards this would make a a good sized lounge, however with the main living room next door this forms a fabulous sitting room, a study, a playroom or other family room. There is a nice fireplace which houses an electric fire and the bow window looks across the fields and takes in those wonderful views. Family Kitchen (6.6m x 6.2m) This fabulous family kitchen really does offer the size and space to accommodate the most demanding of families. It does narrow to 4.00 metres at the dining area. It is extensively fitted with a range of base and wall units, drawers, a central island and work surfaces. There is a large range cooker beneath a canopied hood, and a large dining area overlooking the rear gardens. Double French doors lead out to the patio area, making this a wonderful room for the summer when considering barbecues or other family get-togethers. Utility Room (4.3m x 2.8m) In most houses this would make a good sized kitchen but here it's used as a utility room and, with another door out to the rear gardens, makes for a really useful space. There is a doorway into the garage from this room, too. Cloakroom A more formal cloakroom with plenty of space for coats and shoes, this room is fitted with a white two piece suite consisting of a low level WC and a wash basin and it is also home to the gas boiler. First Floor Landing A wide, atrium style landing with a large roof light allowing plenty of light. There is a small seating area surrounded by bookshelves and eaves access for storage. Bedroom One (4.8m x 4.5m) A good sized principle bedroom which is fitted with an extensive range of wardrobes and drawers. French doors lead out to a private balcony which looks out across to the fields and far off to the distant moors. En-Suite Bathroom A fabulous full bathroom which has a large square bath, a walk in shower with rainwater shower and wand fitments in addition to a heated towel rail, a low level WC and a wash basin set into a four drawer vanity unit. This really is a great feature of this home, and rounds off the principle bedroom suite beautifully. Bedroom Two (4.8m x 2.7m) Another large double room looking out to the front and therefore with those far reaching views. There's plenty of space for wardrobes and other furniture in here, too. En-Suite Bathroom Another full bathroom, this one fitted with a white three piece suite consisting of a low level WC, a wash basin and a bath which has rainwater and wand shower fittings to a shower screen, part tiled walls and a tiled floor. There are useful vanity cupboards and two heated towel rails. Bedroom Three (3.9m x 2.9m) Another double room, this one narrowing slightly to 3.40 metres, overlooking the rear gardens, and with plenty of space for wardrobes and other furniture. En-Suite Bathroom Fitted with a white three piece suite consisting of a low level WC and a wash basin, both set into a vanity unit with cupboards beneath the wash basin, and a bath which has rainwater and wand shower fitments to a shower screen and part tiled walls. Again there is a useful heated towel rail. Bedroom Four Another good double room, this narrowing towards the doorway, overlooking the rear gardens, and again with plenty of space for wardrobes and other furniture. We understand that plans were drawn up to extend this bedroom over the room below to create a guest bedroom suite. Bedroom Five (4.9m x 3.5m) A fifth double bedroom, this narrowing to 3.50 metres, again positioned to the front and taking advantage of those lovely, far reaching views. The room is divided into two areas, one which clearly houses a double bed and the other a dressing area with space for wardrobes. Bathroom This fourth full bathroom is fitted with a three piece suite consisting of a low level WC, a wash basin and a free standing slipper bath. There is also a useful heated towel rail. Additional Information Tenure: Freehold. City of Bradford Council Tax Band: E. Garden The walled gardens to the rear include block paved patio areas and an area of artificial turf. There is a greenhouse for the more green-fingered of us, and a canopied area is currently home to a hot tub which unfortunately will be leaving with the current owners. Parking - Garage The integral garage has light and power and a rear door which leads through to the utility room. Parking - On Drive There is a block paved parking area to the front of the property which will accommodate several cars.

text_description: 'A most impressive period property, offering spacious and versatile living accommodation and delightfully situated in the heart of a much sought-after conservation village. Enjoying an elevated South facing position with views over Heath common this stunning Grade II* listed building is set in fabulous, landscaped grounds of almost 1.5 acres. Dating back to the 1740s and designed by the renowned Yorkshire architect John Carr this stunning property still retains many period features including wood flooring, shutters to the principal rooms, original John Carr oak staircase, period chandelier and intricate hand carvings to the oak panelling. The sale of The Dower House offers an increasingly rare opportunity to acquire what is arguably one of the most significant period residences in the area. The entrance lobby is accessed via the main door to the side courtyard, the ornate panelling, and cornicing gives a fabulous first impression and sets the tone for the wealth of character features found throughout the house. The impressive formal dining room has an open fireplace with stone surround and hearth and a fabulous, feature angled oak staircase leading to the galleried landing. The spacious sitting room has an Adam style fireplace and original timber flooring, connecting to the equally spacious drawing room which has original shutters and a fabulous stone hearth to the log burner. Complementing and delightfully contrasting with these two large rooms is a cosy snug which also has a log burner and the built-in bookcase hides a concealed door to the rear kitchen. The large breakfast kitchen provides access to a private kitchen courtyard and has an ample number of fitted units in the style of Mark Wilkinson, granite worktops and a centre island. The sale includes the gas Aga and integrated appliances include; - dishwasher, fridge, freezer, and additional fridge. The first floor is accessed by two separate staircases, one of which opens up to a stunning galleried landing. The thoughtfully designed layout of six bedrooms provides four of them with en-suite facilities via clever Jack and Jill arrangements, the two principal bedrooms both access a stunning en-suite with a feature Victoria and Albert free standing roll top bath and a separate shower room. The sixth bedroom has fitted wardrobes and connecting to both the main bedroom and the galleried landing it would make an ideal dressing room if so desired. The second floor is currently separated into four additional rooms, having exposed roof timbers and providing access to a private roof terrace this offers huge potential for significant additional living space and would make an ideal study or play area. To the lower ground floor there are extensive cellars with stone flagged flooring ideal for use as a wine cellar or workshop space. Externally to the front of the property there is a large lawned garden with borders well stocked with established plants and bushes, a listed ha-ha marks the boundary to the common. The side courtyard provides off-street parking and leads to the garage and stable block which has fitted light and power and the potential for further garage space. A particular feature of The Dower House is a sperate, enclosed garden set within a predominantly walled boundary, extending to approximately 1 acre the mature trees provide a high degree of privacy making this the perfect area for relaxing or hosting a family celebration of gathering. The historic village of Heath enjoys a fabulous rural setting and is well paced for local and regional commuting, the motorway network is just a short 5-10 minute drive away. Wakefield City Centre is within easy travelling distance and offers a wide range of shops, restaurants and two train stations with regular services to Leeds, London and most major towns and cities. In addition to well-regarded local schools Wakefield is home to the excellent private schools of wghs and qegs. As you enter the village of Heath from Wakefield drive past the Common and turn right and fork immediate left. The Kings Arms public house will be visible on your right and the Dower House is positioned straight ahead to your left.'

text_description: 'It is rare to find a gem of a property that exceeds your expectations - this superb, six bedroom, period terraced home is one such property! This stunning property cannot fail to impress from the moment you walk through the door. It offers the perfect blend of period features including high ceilings, cornicing, picture rails and ceiling roses and full height replacement double-glazed windows combined with quality floorings and contemporary, bespoke, designer fittings all adding to the appeal. Briefly, the accommodation comprises as follows: A wrought-iron gate with matching railings frames a Yorkshire stone path with large, Yorkshire stone patio to one side and leads to steps and an imposing heavy, black, front door, which opens to a porch with tiled flooring. A stripped pine door with beautiful, glazed, leaded panels leads into a welcoming hallway with oak effect flooring. A stripped pine door opens into a truly magnificent sitting room with bay window to the front affording ample natural light. One’s eyes are drawn to a working cast-iron fireplace with black, slate surround and stunning, period features including deep cornicing, picture rail and ceiling rose. A central staircase leads to the first floor and a further stripped pine door opens into a wonderful, bespoke, hand-made dining kitchen by ‘Eastburn Pine’ having solid wooden units, Rangemaster range and central island with travertine marble floor tiling and underfloor heating. Stairs from the kitchen lead down to a utility room and a most spacious family room, which could also be a fabulous dining room. There is ample space for a twelve-seater table and one can imagine many happy times here entertaining friends and family. An original, black, cast-iron range by J & H Smith of Leeds has been fully restored and is a charming focal point. One leads through to a cosy additional family room, currently used as a cinema room with external access to the front patio. Stairs from the hallway lead to the first-floor landing where one finds three immaculately presented double bedrooms, including the master with newly fitted en-suite and a further new shower room. A flight of stairs leads to the second floor where one is not disappointed to find three further double bedrooms and an absolutely stunning, spacious designer wet room. To the front of the property is a south-west facing Yorkshire stone patio with ample space for relaxing and al fresco entertaining, benefitting from sunshine from early afternoon until sunset. Privacy is maintained by well-maintained hedging. There is also private car parking for two cars. The immaculately presented accommodation with gas fired central heating, sealed unit double glazing and with approximate room sizes comprises: Ground Floor Entrance Porch As you approach the property one’s eyes cannot help but admire the handsome façade of this short row of Victorian properties. A Yorkshire stone pathway with a couple of stone steps lead up to a solid, black, painted door which opens into an entrance porch with practical, tiled flooring. Reception Hallway An original stripped pine door with beautiful, leaded, stained-glass panels opens into the spacious reception hallway - ideal for welcoming friends and family. Oak effect flooring and covered radiator. Central stairs to the first floor. Lounge (5.2 x 4.6 (17\'0" x 15\'1")) It is not often you walk into a reception room with perfect proportions. Firstly, a large, tall, bay window with double glazing allows natural light to flood in. The proportions are highlighted by deep cornicing, picture rail and ceiling rose and one’s eyes are drawn to the stunning, cast-iron, real fire with black slate surround and black, ceramic, tiled hearth. The fireplace is flanked either side with built-in cupboards and display shelving. Oak effect flooring, stripped pine door and radiator. Dining Kitchen (5.8 x 4.3 (19\'0" x 14\'1")) One is met by a stunning, handmade, wooden kitchen by ‘Eastburn Pine.’ The subtle, hand painted, ‘Shaker’ style blends perfectly with this beautiful home. Having a range of wall, base and tall pantry style units with a mixture of black, granite and solid wood worksurfaces, incorporating a white, Villeroy & Boch ceramic sink with boiling water tap. A new Professional Deluxe Rangemaster oven with a five-plate induction hob takes pride of place. A large, central island incorporates a breakfast bar with solid oak wood worksurface and useful drawers and cupboards. A large, American style, stainless-steel fridge is set within tall, pantry style cupboards and an integrated dishwasher completes the appliances. Travertine, marble floor tiles with underfloor heating also a selection of oak parquet flooring is a welcome addition and three large windows afford ample natural light. The deep cornicing and picture rail form a charming, eclectic mix with pin-light style downlighting and tall, stainless-steel, designer radiator. There is ample room for a large family dining table and once can imagine many happy times here entertaining friends and family. A further ingenious addition – an invaluable bonus in a busy, family home – are the floor to ceiling, contemporary, fitted, ‘locker’ style cupboards along the width of one wall, providing excellent storage for the usual family paraphernalia, with capacity for even the largest of families to claim their own personal locker space! A section of oak, parquet flooring is an attractive feature. Lower Hallway Stairs from the kitchen lead down to the lower ground floor. Utility Room A useful separate utility room having a good amount of storage with sink and space and plumbing for a separate washing machine and drier underneath a laminate worksurface. Dining/Family Room (5.9 x 3.9 (19\'4" x 12\'9")) A most spacious dining room with engineered oak flooring. This room is currently used as a games room however would easily serve as a formal dining room with ample space to seat twelve at a large, family dining table! An original, black, cast-iron range by J & H Smith of Leeds has been fully restored and is a charming focal point. Having a half-glazed UPVC door with obscure glazed, double-glazed panel giving external access to the rear of the property with further side-window. Designer radiator and downlighting. The room flows through towards the sitting room with a most useful storage cupboard. Family/Cinema Room (4.4 x 3.8 (14\'5" x 12\'5")) A further cosy reception room, an ideal space for the family to relax together or for teenagers to hang out with their friends. Engineered oak flooring and built in storage. An electric stove stands within an open fireplace on a Yorkshire stone hearth. A further designer radiator adds to the contemporary feel. A UPVC door gives access to an external flight of stairs to the front patio. Note It would be possible to convert the lower ground floor into a separate living space with private external access subject to planning approval. First Floor Landing Carpeted stairs lead up to the first-floor landing, again with charming, period features giving access to the principal rooms. Master Bedroom (3.8 x 3.7 (12\'5" x 12\'1")) A wonderful, double bedroom – an oasis of peace and calm with oak effect flooring and most generous, bespoke, contemporary, fitted wardrobes affording plentiful storage enhanced by a further built-in wardrobe. Original, cast-iron fireplace, picture rail and radiator. A large, double-glazed window affords long distance views down the valley. En-Suite Shower Room A concealed sliding door gives access to a recently fitted, stylish and contemporary shower room incorporating a large, fully tiled shower cubicle with mains thermostatic shower and glazed door, a concealed cistern, low-level w/c with push button flush and a wall mounted basin with monobloc tap. Stylish, brick effect, white tiling with attractive, teal coloured contrasting tiling. Painted white floorboards, slim, chrome, ladder, towel radiator and extractor. A large, UPVC double-glazed window with obscure glazing allows for ample natural light. Bedroom Two (4.2 x 3.7 (13\'9" x 12\'1")) This is a charming, double bedroom again having perfect proportions and period features to include a delightful, cast-iron, bedroom fireplace, deep cornicing and picture rail. A UPVC double-glazed window affords views up to the moors and allows the sunlight to flood in. Oak effect flooring and radiator. Bedroom Three (4.2 x 2.3 (13\'9" x 7\'6")) A further double bedroom with oak effect flooring, radiator and double-glazed window with window seat overlooking the front garden and the moors beyond. Family Shower Room A further double bedroom with oak effect flooring, radiator and double-glazed window with window seat overlooking the front garden and the moors beyond. Second Floor Landing A door gives access to a further flight of carpeted stairs leading to the second-floor landing. An under stairs cupboard provides useful linen storage. Bedroom Four (5.5 x 3.1 (18\'0" x 10\'2")) A further spacious, double bedroom with fitted wardrobes, exposed roof truss, oak effect flooring, radiator and Velux windows affording stunning, far reaching, countryside views. Bedroom Five (4.3 x 3.2 (14\'1" x 10\'5")) A charming, double bedroom having fitted wardrobes, oak effect flooring, exposed roof truss and a Velux window affording stunning views. Fitted desk with useful shelving above. Radiator with cover. A loft hatch with pull down ladder gives access to a large, boarded out loft space with light. Bedroom Six (4.1 x 2.8 (13\'5" x 9\'2")) Last, but not least, no-one draws the short straw in this home - a double room, with exposed beam, radiator and oak effect flooring. A charming, arched window affords ample natural light and lovely, far reaching views. Designer Wet Room Just when you have thought you have seen everything, one opens the stripped pine door and finds an absolutely stunning designer wet room having a fully tiled travertine floor and most spacious, walk-in wet room, with thermostatic drench shower and glazed screen. Open to the roof space, this is a wonderful room. A Velux window affords natural light. A traditional basin has a mosaic, tiled splashback and lit-mirror, low-level w/c and useful, built-in storage. Exposed roof truss and chrome, ladder, towel radiator. There is ample space to add a free-standing bath should one wish (with plumbing in place). Outside Patio Garden To the front of the property is a spacious, Yorkshire stone flagged area, ideal for relaxing or al fresco entertaining with good friends and privacy is maintained by tall hedging. This area is flooded with sunshine from early afternoon to sunset. Hence ‘Sunset Drive’. The property benefits from two private, off-road parking spaces. Council Tax City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council Tax Band F.'

Netherton is a popular and convenient semi-rural village with varied local amenities, schooling for younger children and a local bus services too. Well placed for access to the wider amenities on hand across the Holme Valley and Huddersfield. One can even access the Colne Valley, where there are local railway stations connecting to Leeds and Manchester. The nearest railway stations in Berry Brow & Honley have a Huddersfield to Sheffield line, making this an excellent base for families and business travellers. The house is well appointed with modern attractive fixtures and fittings. The bathroom, two en-suites and ground floor w.c. All have white sanitary ware and well chosen tiling and floorings. Other highlights include the large lounge with an impressive fireplace and inset stove, spacious breakfast dining kitchen with attractive units, granite worktops and integrated appliances, and the impressive and welcoming reception hall which has a galleried landing above. A snug with a mezzanine over offers flexibility as a play room, guest sitting room or home office. A ground floor bedroom with fitted wardrobes and en-suite shower room is presently used as a playroom for younger children. A dining room, integral double garage, utility room, cloakroom/wc and home office/study complete the ground floor. On the first floor are three double bedrooms and a side room which is an ideal dressing room and potentially bedroom 5. There is a lovely family bathroom including a separate shower and bath, and also an en-suite bathroom and fitted wardrobes to the master bedroom. View our floor plan and 3D tour to gain an understanding of the varied and extensive layout before arranging a personal viewing. The house has a gas central heating system, double glazing and a burglar alarm. Viewing is highly recommended to avoid disappointment. The essentials: The house is Freehold. Mains services are available. Council Tax Band F.'

text_description: Sowerby Bridge is full of surprises, and this is one of them; a small terrace of spacious Victorian homes in a gorgeous setting. With barely any passing traffic, surrounded by woodland and overlooking allotments it feels very tucked away, yet in reality it's just a stone's throw to Trinity Academy Grammar School and all the facilities Sowerby Bridge has to offer. Those include great pubs, restaurants and a choice of large supermarkets, a modern sports centre and the railway station, with regular connections to both Leeds and Manchester. If you commute by car, Halifax and the M62 are easily accessed too. The house itself has been a much-loved family home for many years and is now a little dated. But it's big, offering over 1300 square feet of living space, with the potential for more. There's some really nice period features, and a new kitchen, some replastering and redecoration would work wonders. Set over four floors there's four double bedrooms and the bathroom on the upper floors, plus a good-sized living room and kitchen-dining room on the ground floor. On the lower ground floor the cellar offers a huge opportunity. Having been used as a large workshop / utility room for many years there's potential to re-open an unused room to double the available space. Perhaps you'd like a games room, gym, your own home cinema or spacious playroom? Starting our tour at the front door, there's a small lobby area before entering the living room. Here there's an art deco-style gas fire, plus attractive coving to the ceiling and a picture rail, all adding character to the room. To the rear a door opens into a small inner hallway and then into the large kitchen-dining room. You'll want to replace the kitchen, but there's plenty of space for a range of units plus a good-sized dining table too, making for a really good layout well-suited to family life or entertaining friends for dinner. A door leads down into the large cellar, which is dry and has been used for many years as a workshop and laundry room (power, water and drainage are all laid-on). The rest of the cellar space, running all the way under the living room, has been shut off, but there's potential to re-open this space and bring it back into use, creating a huge amount of extra reception space. Back upstairs, stairs lead up from the inner hallway to the first floor, where there are two double bedrooms and the bathroom. The main bedroom is huge, with great views near and far from the window and plenty of room to add a shower room if you wish. The second bedroom is smaller, but also a double, again with lovely views, this time over woodland to the rear. Next door is the bathroom, which is modern and perfectly usable. Up the stairs again and we come to the 2nd floor, with another two double bedrooms. To the front the larger room has a big dormer window, ensuring maximum headroom and again with potential for an ensuite. The rear bedroom is a smaller double set into the eaves, light and bright thanks to the large roof window. Finally the outdoor space. The front of the house faces south and has great views and there's a good sized space here ideal for a table and chairs plus a few pots. To the back of the house a door opens from the kitchen-dining room onto a smaller yard, perfect for outdoor storage and hanging the washing. There's access for cars to the rear of the terrace, and just across the access track is a slightly elevated garden area with a wooded backdrop, making a very pleasant spot to relax. To summarise, while the house requires some work to bring it back to it's best, there's great potential here to put your stamp on it and create a really large family home. The location is both very convenient and in many ways idyllic - quiet and with gorgeous surroundings. Opportunities like this don't come up often, so give us a ring, 24/7 for further information and to book your place to view! Some further practicalities: The house is fully double-glazed with gas central heating throughout. Parking is on the street outside the house. text_description: 'Old Beck Farm has a handsome, stone built period farm house and outbuildings set in the centre of its land in a beautiful rural setting with convenient local connections. The property provides more than 7000 square feet of flexible accommodation, offering considerable development potential (subject to planning) which could be configured into three separate dwellings, including holiday lets or accommodation for a dependant relative. The farmhouse has a wealth of charming period features, including exposed timber beams, stone and brickwork, vaulted ceilings and original fireplaces. The main house has five flexible, comfortable reception rooms, including a sitting room, dining room, breakfast room, an office and a home gym, while the large kitchen is an excellent social space, with flagstone flooring, a central island and an Aga. The second ground floor living space has a fully equipped cinema room with a stunning vaulted ceiling, a further reception room and a kitchen. The first floor offers three large double bedrooms, including the principal bedroom with a luxury en-suite bathroom and stunning views to the south. There’s also a family bathroom with Jacuzzi bath, while the second floor has an office, which could be used as a further large double bedroom. The property is in a peaceful rural setting, to the south side of Burley Moor, a location from where this rural haven enjoys stunning views to the south along with ready access to the nearby towns of Ilkley and Guiseley. 12 miles from Leeds city centre, surrounded by beautiful rolling North Yorkshire countryside. Local amenities can be found in the town of Guiseley, three miles away, including a range of shops, supermarket, leisure facilities and Guiseley train station. The nearest primary school is in nearby Hawksworth, while the outstanding-rated secondary St. Mary’s Menston, and is less than three miles away along with Menston train station which has free parking. The vibrant city of Leeds also provides a wealth of excellent shops, leisure and cultural facilities, large supermarkets, as well as a world-class educational facilities, including the University of Leeds. The area is well connected by road, with a-roads leading to Leeds. Otley and Ilkley are only a short drive away offering an array of independent shops and businesses. The property is set in the centre of its extensive private grounds approached along a private driveway, with open countryside views, fields and paddocks, ideal for equestrian use or for raising livestock. The south-facing walled garden is laid to lawn, with border flowerbeds and paved pathways and terracing. The cobbled central courtyard provides parking space for several vehicles. The stone barn provides a wealth of storage, in addition to this there is also a hard-core track leading to a large hard standing area which can be used for further parking of machinery. The property enjoys Woodlands, landscaped gardens along with a vegetable garden and orchard. Also nearby a delightful stream with small waterfall.'

Viewings are available by appointment only. The Pantiles, is one of those opportunities, which rarely comes along in North Leeds. Even rarer, is to find such a high standard of property chain free in such a sought-after location. Enjoying an enviable 1⁄4 Acre plot and internal footprint of 3,200 Sqft, this home has been newly renovated throughout and is ideally located for those seeking excellent access to Moorlands School, David Lloyd and The Hollies. You arrive at this substantial property and the vendors have recently improved the frontage with electric gates and an extended driveway. Briefly, the main house comprises of a reception hall which accommodates a guest WC and cloakroom, leading through to a large kitchen/diner and a utility room, just off of the integral garage. The formal living room offers 510 Sqft in total and leads, To the first floor, there are 5 bedrooms, a bathroom, a shower room, and a separate w.c. The Annex can form part of the main house if required. It is accessed from the formal living room but it also has its own separate access. The annex briefly comprises:- entrance porch, vestibule, Sitting room, Breakfast kitchen, and shower room, all to the ground floor, which makes for a fantastic guest accommodation or may suit multiple generations living together. There are 6 double bedrooms on the first floor, two of which benefit from en suite shower rooms. There are two brand new modernised house bathrooms to the upstairs. This home benefits from a gas fired central heating system and all windows are double glazed. Set back from Foxhill Avenue and with a frontage of over 120 feet, and a depth varying from 80 to 100 feet, this is a generous 1⁄4 Acre corner plot, which provides great outdoor space for those who like to entertain or enjoy the outdoor life. The garden benefits from new decking, perfect for entertaining. The main arterial roads give easy access to Horsforth, Moortown, Chapel Allerton, Headingley, and Bramhope. Leeds city centre and access to the motorway networks, and of course, Leeds and Bradford International Airport is a few miles away. Public transport is on hand and there is a selection of schools in proximity, catering for children of all ages. Private schooling and nurseries too. Apart from good shopping, restaurants, pubs, and wine bars, there are lots of sports clubs to visit in order to work off those over indulgencies; The Village, David Lloyds and Chapel Allerton Lawn Tennis and Squash Club to name just a few. Also of local interest, is Golden Acre Park, The Canal Gardens at Roundhay, and the famous Roundhay Park with its' twin lakes. Oh, and don't forget The Meanwood Valley Trail too. There are at least 6 good golf courses within a few miles. So...lots to do! Viewings are available by appointment only.

text_description: Set in the sought-after village of Adel, Preston Baker are delighted to introduce this exclusive five-bedroom detached home to the market on Adel Vale with no chain! Situated just five miles from Leeds City Centre, Adel is a beautiful mixture of rural and urban living. The location of the village makes it perfect for commuting but is still tucked away enough to enjoy a peaceful, rural lifestyle close to the country. With excellent schooling and amenities close by, Adel is an extremely sought after location to be in North Leeds with everything it has to offer. This property has been renovated and extended twice over the years to it's current glory - perfect for modern, open-plan family living. On entering the property, you are greeted with a light and airy hallway; leading off to the left is the main lounge area with an abundance of space. The wall to the end of the lounge has been knocked through, creating a real feel of space throughout and follows through to the kitchen dining area. Separate to the kitchen is a further utility space, and access to the larger-than-average double garage, which has all been recently re-roofed. Adjoining the playroom, there is a generously-sized downstairs double bedroom with three-piece en-suite. Furthermore, there is also a downstairs W/C. Upstairs, are three further double-bedrooms and one single bedroom. The master-suite has been extended further, adding a walk-in dressing room and further wet-room, three-piece en-suite. Both the master and adjoining double bedroom both feature fitted wardrobes and dressing tables, allowing for plenty of storage throughout. The three-piece family bathroom has been modernised to an exceptional standard. Externally, the property is situated on a large plot that offers a mass of space. Privately situated at the end of the cul-de-sac, the plot is extremely tranquil, perfect to relax and watch the world go by, mainly laid to lawn with easy to maintain borders. The property benefits further from a block-paved driveway which is easily capable of providing parking for four plus cars leading to further parking/storage space in the double garage. Due to the sought-after location and sheer size of this beautiful family home, a physical viewing is highly recommended to appreciate what this rare-to-the-market home has to offer!

text_description: What an amazing home! Set on Royd Crescent, a popular cul-de-sac less than five minutes walk from Mytholmroyd railway station, commuting by bus, train or car from here is a breeze. There's also easy access to numerous beautiful walks and the cycle path linking Mytholmroyd with Hebden Bridge and Sowerby Bridge, making this a real \x91best of both worlds' location. It's a quiet spot with views across the valley and a super-friendly local community too. The sizeable front garden sits behind a neat fence, and is a brilliant feature of the property. There's a patio close to the house and a lawn with mature planting thoughtfully chosen to provide an abundance of flowers and colour throughout the year. The house itself is semi-detached with attractive 1930s details such as a mullioned square bay window and panelled front door with stained glass. Inside, original stripped wood doors paired with tasteful Farrow and Ball décor make for a colourful yet very tranquil feel. Stepping through the front door there's a small lobby area, perfect for hanging your coat before moving further into the house. A door to the left opens into the living room, beautifully decorated to accentuate the chimney breast and plasterwork. Deep coving to the ceiling and a picture rail add to the period charm, and the woodburning stove makes this a cosy spot to gather and watch a movie as the mercury drops outside. The bay window is huge with a gorgeous curved wall to each side, making the room beautifully light whatever the weather. A door leads onwards into the extended kitchen - dining room, which is a really good size. The kitchen boasts a large gas range cooker and built-in dishwasher, plus there's space for a washing machine and fridge freezer too. With plenty of workspace it's a practical layout perfect for the keen (or more reluctant!) cook. The dining room extends directly off the kitchen to create an L shape, making this a very sociable home ideal for entertaining friends and family with drinks and a meal. Just behind the dining area doors open into a good-sized sunroom complete with underfloor heating. With floor to ceiling glass on two sides there's a real feeling of bringing the outside space in, and more than enough room for a sofa. Alternatively how about using this space as a home office? Upstairs there are two double bedrooms and the bathroom. Starting with bedroom one, this is a very large double room, beautifully decorated and with far-reaching views. There's plenty of room for a large double bed, plus a built in wardrobe alongside the chimney breast and walk-in cupboard over the stairs providing excellent storage. Next door, bedroom two is a smaller double, but would make a perfect guest bedroom / study or children's room. Finally, the bathroom has striking black and white tiling to the floor and is brightly lit thanks to the large window. There's a WC, basin and large bath perfect for a relaxing soak, with an overhead shower for when you're in more of a hurry. Things are kept nice and toasty by a Victorian-style towel radiator. Outside, an L shaped rear patio garden wraps around the sun room and alongside the kitchen extension. Facing east, you'll get the morning sun here, ideal for a quick morning cuppa or lazy brunch. Meanwhile the larger garden to the front of the house faces west, making this the place for relaxing during the afternoon and into the evening. There's a small patio close to the house and a larger stretch of lawn with mature planting providing great colour and privacy. A few extra practicalities: Parking is available on the private road, or it should be possible to use part of the front garden to create a driveway if preferred. The house is fully double-glazed and heating is provided by a gas combination boiler (with electric underfloor heating in the sunroom). A loft with drop-down ladder offers excellent further storage in the roof space. So, in summary, this is a handsome and very well presented home which makes a real impression. It's in a perfect location, right on the doorstep of central Mytholmroyd, yet in a quiet position tucked away from the main road. Room sizes are excellent and there's great garden space too. Ticking so many boxes, we're expecting plenty of interest in this lovely property. So don't delay - give us a call now, 24/7, and book your place to view. text_description: 'Cherry Tree Cottage is a truly individual, stone built, four double bedroom detached property with level garden and cobbled driveway for two cars in the heart of the vibrant village of Burley in Wharfedale. This is a rare opportunity to purchase such a delightful, family home. A solid timber entrance door opens into a charming hall with attractive tiled flooring with space for coats and shoes. Pine doors lead into a comfortable lounge with shutters to the large window overlooking the fore garden and the open plan living dining kitchen with impressive log burning stove and patio doors leading out to the rear garden. text_description: 'A stunning Victorian stone built residence of significant charm and quality, situated in a highly desirable residential location in Baildon within a short walk of the railway station. Offering four bedrooms, ground floor W.C, spacious open plan kitchen diner, stylish house bathroom and gardens with parking area. An inspection is highly advised to fully appreciate this wonderful period home. We are delighted to offer to the market this charming and characterful period mews cottage forming part of what was once a much larger property "Ingfield" originally built in the late 18th Century. The house has been subject to comprehensive improvements by the current owners and now offers beautifully presented family accommodation matching an enviable specification with the endearing character of the period. Planned over three floors the property briefly comprises on the ground floor; day room/spacious hallway with multi-fuel stove; access to cellar; W.C.; living room with feature stone wall; spacious open plan kitchen diner with dining area and access to the garden; staircase leading to the first floor. On the first floor; three generous bedrooms; study with fitted storage; spacious house bathroom with freestanding bath and walk-in shower; staircase leading to the second floor; On the second floor; further good sized bedroom with velux windows and eaves storage (building regulations approved). There is a large vaulted cellar on the lower ground floor providing a useful storage space. The property also benefits from a gas fired heating system and double glazing. Externally, there is a cobbled parking area for three vehicles, and a delightful enclosed garden with a Yorkshire stone flagged patio leading to a lawn surrounded by decorative borders, hedging and timber fencing. Gated access leading down to Kirklands Road. Baildon is a popular village which offers a wide variety of amenities including shops, restaurants and recreational facilities including a golf course, rugby, cricket and football grounds. Baildon has a rural location with moorland countryside close by as well as allowing daily commuting by rail to Leeds and Bradford. Motorway and air networks are also within easy reach. The area is also close to the World Heritage site of Saltaire and to the green corridor of the Leeds Liverpool Canal with its scenic walks and national cycle path. From the roundabout in the centre of Baildon proceed down Browgate, at Threshfield crossroads turn left into Station Road, after approximately one mile turn right into Kirklands Road and Ingfield is the first private turning on the left hand side. The property is located towards the end of the mews on the right hand side.'

text_description: 'Initial description Nicely tucked away and enjoying a good amount of privacy and seclusion, is this substantial 5 bedroomed detached residence. It is also suited to young families being within walking distance of all the local schools. About quarry house We understand that the property was constructed around 1840 by the owner of a nearby quarry. Over the years it has been occupied by various families including a doctor who also ran his surgery from here. The property was later divided into two homes until the current owners bought it in 1985 at which point they returned it to a single residence. It is now time for its next chapter and ready to welcome a new family who will lovingly refurbish it to their own taste and style and enjoy all that Quarry House has to offer. The accommodation briefly comprises front entrance porch giving way to the main hall which is over 36\' long, 3 large reception rooms, conservatory, dining kitchen, utility with w.c., and access down to 2 large cellars. Quarry House has a gas fired central heating system, double glazed windows, and a security alarm. Externally, the driveway leads on to a parking and turning area in front of a detached double garage. To the right of this stands Quarry House within extensive gardens comprising lawns, well stocked flower beds, a raised pond, stone patio, raised vegetable beds, fruit bushes, and a variety of fruit trees. The gardens and grounds are then bordered by mature trees and shrubs comprising mainly holly and rhododendron which were highly favoured by the Victorians during the period the house was built. The property is not far from the village centres of either Linthwaite, Slaithwaite or Meltham where you will find an array of amenities, and is within walking distance of Colne Valley High School and regular bus routes. Situated in the popular village of North Rigton, five miles to the south west of Harrogate, this 17th century farm cottage and attached barn has been much updated by the present owners to provide versatile living spaces with private outdoor terraces and well stocked gardens. The property has original features in abundance including beamed ceilings, an inglenook fireplace and reclaimed timber flooring. Reclaimed, hand-made tiles with underfloor heating feature throughout. The property is ideally situated for short commutes by car to Leeds and Harrogate and is an easy 1.2 miles from Weeton railway station on the Leeds, Harrogate, York line. The ground floor accommodation comprises: Front entrance hall leading to a light-filled vaulted ceiling open plan kitchen/dining room with bespoke oak kitchen cabinets, three oven Aga, large walk in pantry and unrestricted views of open countryside. Double doors give access to York stone outdoor living spaces and rear garden. Steps lead up to the living room with original inglenook open fire and to the snug, which doubles as a fourth bedroom when required and features original beams, fire surround and wood burning stove. There is a generous storeroom with access to the oil central heating boiler. A short corridor from the living room to the study provides access to the utility room and downstairs shower room/wc. The study offers dual aspect views of the Wharfe Valley and the private rear garden. Stairs lead to three double bedrooms: The master bedroom has a vaulted ceiling and an en-suite with a roll top bath with overhead shower and countryside views. Bedroom two is generously proportioned and has an en-suite shower room. Bedroom three overlooks the rear garden. text_description: 'With parts dating back to the 1800\'s, Chapel Barn is filled with rustic character, fused with modern provisions including a multi fuel wood burning stove, under floor heating throughout with zone controls and ensuite facilities in one of the 3 bedrooms. Entering the property into an internal glass fronted porch which streams in natural light into the dining kitchen, you encounter a great space to decloak before entering the main property. With fitted blinds, the property has a ceramic floor which flows from the porch and into the dining kitchen. The spacious kitchen has room for a dining table and is well equipped with a bank of wall and base cabinets. The house bathroom has a large bath with mixer shower above, wash basin with drawer unit and low level w.c. Partially tiled with a combination of white and grey with a chrome trim, the room is completed with a chrome towel radiator. Exterior In a quiet hamlet, Rookery Farm is a residential setting, surrounded by countryside. Chapel Barn is at the end of the hamlet with no passing traffic and includes a detached single garage with two parking spaces. text_description: 'Description Victorian grandeur, embracing spaces and beguiling views combine at Estate House, a unique and imposing home, conveniently close to transport links yet serenely set in the sought-after village of West Bretton. Victorian splendour Built in the mid 1800s, the Grade-ii listed, double fronted home formerly served the estate officers for Bretton parkland farms. A home that wraps itself around you, Estate House has been renovated and reloved by its current owners, whilst retaining many handsome original features. To the rear, a shared driveway leads to an area of designated parking for two or three cars. Everyday access can be found to the rear, via the utility room, but for the full wow-factor arrival, make your way to the main front entrance, where glazed double doors open to the impressive entrance hall. A warm welcome Step inside, onto the flagstone original flooring and sense the duality of this unique home; light and airy, the double height ceiling rises up above whilst the solid, thick walls wrap around you creating an instant sense of separation from the world outside. A home made for Christmas and celebrations, dress the entrance hall with an eight-foot tree during the festive season for a warm and welcoming arrival home. Turning right, discover the decadent dining room, with tray ceiling stretching up above. An electric fire adds ambience within its stone surround, with an abundance of storage found within the fitted cabinets to either side. Entertain with ease Easily seating 14 around the lengthy dining table, this room embodies the sociable side of Estate House; a home most at home when entertaining and resonating with the sound of conversation and laughter. Owner quote: "This home can soak up people. We\'ve had a party for 100 people, but equally when you\'re in on your own it feels so cosy and safe." Solid, robust walls retain the heat in wintertime, whilst keeping cool in summertime. An all-season home, in autumn, swish through the leaves in the park to the rear. From the entrance hall, continue ahead into the rear hall, where there is a handy cloakroom with wash basin and WC for guests, before turning left into the living room. Relax and unwind Tall, shuttered sash windows draw copious light through to the living room, framing verdant views out to the garden. So spacious, fill this room with family and friends or enjoy the comfort and protection of its solid design on cosy evenings in. Polished wood flooring extends underfoot, whilst warmth emanates from the ornamental electric fire set within its handsome stone surround. Ample storage can be found in the original arched, fitted alcove cabinetry fitted to either side of the chimney breast. Imagine installing a hearty log-burning stove for those chilly winter nights... Owner quote: "I love the openness, on a gloomy dark day the ceilings are so high you just feel you have space and light, it\'s so tranquil." Feast your eyes Returning to the rear hall, freshen up in the guest cloakroom with WC, wash basin and window, before making your way through to the kitchen on the right. Feast your eyes on this light, bright and sociable room, where tall white cabinetry offers ample storage to the side, also accommodating a large freestanding American-style fridge-freezer. Chat and share a glass of wine with the chef at the breakfast bar, where there is seating for four beneath the contemporary pendant lighting. Plenty of storage is available in the large pantry to the rear. Brimming with cupboards throughout the home, storage is a key motif at Estate House. Cook up a dinner to savour on the double Range-style oven with gas hob. Integrated appliances include a dishwasher whilst in the utility room, discover plumbing for a washer and dryer and practical tiled flooring ideal for four legged friends. Direct access is available from here to the parking at the rear. From the kitchen, sneak a peek at the cellar, accessible down a set of stairs. Artistic designs... After dinner, relax in the sitting room, a cosy and versatile room that has previously served as a breakfast room, playroom, painting studio and office. A place to sit and ponder, light fills the room from the tall sash windows, framing pretty views out to the surrounds. With a thriving art scene in and around Wakefield, the large walls of Estate House are blank canvases upon which to display your favourite works. Returning to the entrance hall, ascend the carpeted, kite winding staircase to the impressive galleried landing with oak balustrade. Soak & sleep Turning left, make your way to the main bedroom, a capacious room swimming in light courtesy of a large window to the side and another large, shuttered sash window to the front overlooking the cenotaph, a focal point in West Bretton. Carpeted in cream and with elegant cornicing to the ceiling, uplighting adds a subtle glow. Ample storage is available in the walk-in wardrobe furnished with hanging space and shelving, whilst refreshment awaits in the luxurious ensuite, with wash basin, bath, separate shower, WC and heated towel radiator. Privately set away from the remaining bedrooms, retrace your steps away from the main bedroom and back along the landing to discover a mirror image bedroom also overlooking the front. With a walk-in wardrobe and ensuite bathroom with bath, shower, wash basin, WC and heated towel rail, Estate House is unique in the sense that it offers two equally proportioned principal bedrooms. Continuing along the landing step down to arrive at two further bedrooms, peacefully situated to the rear. Bedroom three, on the right is a comfortable double with open views through windows to rear and side, whilst bedroom four, to the rear, could make an ideal nursery or home office, furnished with fitted storage. All the bedrooms benefit from their original wooden shutters. Serving both these bedrooms is the house bathroom, furnished with panelled bath, separate shower, wash basin and WC. Easy outdoor space Picturesquely set behind lush lawns retained by wrought iron railings, Estate House is every inch the Victorian manor house. Easily maintained, handsome Yorkshire stone paving leads around the side to the rear garden where there is scope for a seating area with table and chairs. On your doorstep Step outside and get to know the delightful and much sought-after village of West Bretton. A village with a friendly and traditional feel, sit out on the cricket pavilion in the summer months with a picnic and enjoy the innings. Children are well served by the small yet dynamic, rural primary school, whilst there are several nearby independent schools including Silcoates School, Queen Elizabeth Grammar School and Wakefield Independent School, all less than 20 minutes\' drive away. Explore the local art scene with a visit to The Hepworth Gallery in nearby Wakefield, only seven miles away, or closer to home with a stroll around the beautiful Yorkshire Sculpture Park, only two minutes down the road. Less than ten minutes\' drive away head to The Three Acres inn and restaurant, a popular spot for dining and socialising. Pick up your artisanal produce from the Blacker Hall Farm Shop nearby and stay for coffee and cake in the café. In the grounds of Bretton Park there is also a café. Only a stone\'s throw from J38 of the M1 and the M62; Estate House is so conveniently placed for commuting into London, Leeds, Manchester and across to the West. Catch a train into London within two hours from the Station at Wakefield Westgate. Enjoy the thriving social scenes of both Leeds and Sheffield, both on your doorstep and less than an hour\'s drive away. For a home that embraces you from the second you step through the door, Estate House balances grandeur with warmth, for a feeling of happiness and security. Book your viewing today. Useful to know: * Grade II listed Building * Council Tax Band H * Wakefield City Council * Freehold * lpg Central Heating * Mains Electric, Water and Drainage Council Tax Band: H Tenure: Freehold'

text_description: Built in 2006 to a high specification, the houses of Longstaff Court are designed to echo mill workers cottages but on a grander scale and with all the benefits of living in a newer property. Mullioned windows and exposed purlins are complemented by a modern finish, creating a stylish home which is easy to heat and maintain yet very appropriate to the surroundings. Located just a few minutes walk from the centre of Hebden Bridge you're right on the doorstep of everything this quirky part of Yorkshire has to offer - the independent shops, cafes, bars and restaurants aren't far and it's only a short stroll to the canal-side and a host of gorgeous countryside walks. For those using public transport there's a bus stop close by, offering services both along the valley and up into the surrounding hills. On approach you'll find the house at the end of a short terrace, with a smart block paved driveway providing off-street parking for two cars. To the left there's entry into a triangular side garden, which wraps around the house to the rear. With a mix of colourful perennials and a lush green lawn this is a lovely space, enclosed and totally private. At the same time it's also very sunny, the dual aspect enjoying the best of the afternoon and evening sunshine - perfect for a pre-dinner tipple as you watch the sun go down. Back to the front of the property and stepping through the front door we enter the house via a useful lobby area, ideal for shedding coats and shoes before heading further inside. Just to the left is the living room, which is a very good size with room to seat the whole family. There's a gas fire in here but, being an end-terrace, it should be possible to install a woodburning stove if you prefer. It's the perfect room for cosy evenings in gathered around the TV! From here a door opens into the very generous kitchen-dining room, making it a modern and practical ground floor layout. This is the real heart of the home, a bright and welcoming room with light flooding in from the rear. The kitchen layout is excellent, with plentiful wall and base units in a neutral shaker style, and contrasting beech worktops for a country feel. To the right is a utility area with space for the washing machine and tumble dryer, while the main kitchen is a large L shape with quality built in appliances - a gas hob, electric oven, dishwasher and fridge-freezer. There's bags of space left over for a large dining table, making it a brilliant space for both cooking and entertaining. To the rear there's a useful downstairs WC, and the back door takes us out into the enclosed rear garden, perfect for dining al-fresco, nipping outside to snip some herbs, or keeping an eye on the kids playing outside. Upstairs the four bedrooms are spread over two floors, One of the real highlights of the property is the very generous bedroom sizes; all are large doubles, neutrally decorated and ready for you to add a splash of colour if you wish. On the middle floor we have the master bedroom with ensuite shower room, which is very well planned to allow space for a large double bed, plus wardrobes all along one wall. From the window there are lovely views towards Horsehold. Next door, bedroom two is another generous double, and the family bathroom is spacious too, with a shower over the bath, WC and basin. It's a relaxing space perfect for a long soak in the bath after a stressful day. On the second floor we find two more very large bedrooms, with space to add another bathroom too if you wish. These rooms are tucked into the eaves but with excellent headroom, and the sloping ceilings and wood purlins add real character. Bedroom three is beautifully bright thanks to light from the large roof window plus low-level mullioned windows running almost along its entire length. Currently used as a craft room this would make a brilliant studio or a wonderful large double bedroom. Next door, bedroom four is even bigger, and offers the opportunity to subdivide and create an extra bathroom, or if you work from home how about splitting it into two generous office spaces? With this much room on offer there's multiple options to adapt the space to suit your needs. So how to summarise this lovely, generously sized home? With excellent room sizes, driveway parking and gardens, plus the fantastic location right on the edge of Hebden Bridge, this is a must-see property. Double glazed and with gas central heating throughout, it has an EPC rating of C, meaning cheaper bills too! We're expecting high demand, so call our friendly team now, 24/7, to arrange your viewing. Auction Date The property will be sold by public auction on Friday, 16 December 2022, via a 2-hour online bidding window. To View The property can be viewed by booking onto one of the advertised managed block viewings. Once you have registered to bid by setting up your online bidding account, you will be emailed a Calendly link to do this. Each block viewing is strictly 30 minutes, and no ad hoc viewings will be available. In most cases, a video tour will be available. This is an immediate and unconditional exchange of contracts with the payment of a 10% deposit of the winning bid and the auction fees for the property. Completion will be confirmed in the V4 Special Conditions in the Legal Pack. It is the bidder’s responsibility to read these and understand the terms and conditions of the auction. Set Up An Online Bidding Account Once you have expressed an interest in the property, you will be emailed a link to set up your online bidding account (this can be found on our website under ‘Auction Lots'. Setting up your bidding account is free, and it is here that you will have access to the legal pack. Once your account is registered, you will be automatically notified of any additions or changes to the legal documents or the auction date/process. Only the bidder needs to register. Should you win the auction, additional buyers can be nominated. Confirm Your Id Once you have set up your online bidding account, we will send you an sms through which you can download the Credas smartphone application to work through the remote confirmation of your id. This will need to be done for all nominated buyers should you win the auction. Please note that should your nominated buyers fail to complete the id checks then you, the bidder, will be noted as the buyer as per the V4 Common Auction Conditions. Read The Legal Documents Each property will have a full set of legal documents available through your online bidding account. The legal pack will contain all the information held on the property, and the V4 Special Conditions will detail the completion date and any additional fees to be paid on completion. Pay The Security Deposit To bid on the day during the 2-hour online bidding window, you will need to pay a security deposit of £5,000. Once your id is confirmed, you will be sent the relevant details to pay the security deposit. This will be paid into our client account using a faster payment /chaps (bacs is unacceptable) via a link we will email you or by card over the phone. This deposit will be returned should the Lot withdraw, you withdraw, or you are unsuccessful. If you are the winning bidder, you will be invoiced for the balance of the 10% deposit and auction fees immediately. There is a £49 incl. VAT processing fee if the security deposit is paid by card via the link or over the phone. Pre-Auction Bids These must be made in writing by email and will only be put to the client once you have set up your online bidding account and confirmed your id as described above. The pre-auction bid will also need to be more than the advertised guide price. Should your pre-auction bid be accepted, you will need to make payment of the 10% deposit and the auction fees immediately. 2-Hour Online Bidding Window The 2-hour online bidding is the modern version of the auction saleroom. Our process is public and transparent. Once your bidding account is set up, your id is confirmed, and you have paid a security deposit, you will be able to bid once the auction opens. We will offer bidding increments, and you can bid higher amounts. The final bid will need to stand for 30 seconds when the auction ends. You will then need to pay the balance of the 10% deposit and auction fees in full and supply a valid conveyancer within 2-working days of the auction ending or the acceptance of a pre-auction bid. Auction Fees In addition to the 10% deposit of your winning bid, you will need to pay 1% plus VAT of the purchase price and £2,500 plus VAT. Please be aware there may be additional fees, including disbursements in the legal pack, payable on completion. Check the legal pack for each lot you are interested in before bidding. A Note On Guide Prices Guide Prices are provided as an indication of each seller's minimum expectation. They do not necessarily set the figure that a lot will sell for and may change at any time before the auction. Each lot will be offered subject to a reserve (a figure below which the auctioneer cannot sell the property during the auction) which will be set within a reasonable bidding range of the stated guide price. Completion The completion date is specified in the V4 Special Conditions contained in the Legal Pack for the property, which can be accessed through your online bidding account. If no date is mentioned in the V4 Special Conditions, the V4 Common Auction Conditions mandate that the completion will be 20-working days from the auction or sooner by agreement. There will be no access to the property allowed before completion except by accredited and insured surveyors, as requested and arranged through us. Upon completion, once the funds are confirmed, the keys will be released by post to the new owner. This can take up to 3 working days.

text_description: Quote TD0438 Tom Donnelly, your personal estate agent, is delighted to market this five bedroom detached dormer bungalow situated on a residential cul-de-sac of exclusive detached homes in the popular village of Lofthouse. Offering more than meets the eye this fabulous home has two floors of living accommodation with two bedrooms on the first floor with a three piece family bathroom offering potential annexe/home office space for those that need it. This amazing home is any downsizer's dream with approximately 2000 square feet of flexible living accommodation and manageable, well maintained gardens to the front and rear. The previous owner was a master craftsman and has spent a huge amount of time installing hardwood panelling to much of the interior downstairs and with some clever use of colour schemes and some interior flair you could really make this an outstanding home and the envy of all your friends. The property is approached via wrought iron gates leading to extensive off street parking and a spacious double garage with electric up and over doors. The entrance hall is welcoming and three of five bedrooms are located downstairs. The master bedroom is particularly impressive with ample room for a king size and includes custom fitted wardrobes. The second bedroom is a comfortable double and also benefits from fitted wardrobes. Bedroom three is an ideal hobby/crafts room and is currently used as an office/snug. The 19’ x 12’ living kitchen is vast and accommodating and solves one of the common problems with downsizing which is not having the open plan living space for entertaining guests. In need of some cosmetic updating the kitchen has stood the test of time wonderfully well and the quality of the craftsmanship is undeniable. There is a convenient and practical utility room tucked just off this space and is ideal for white goods to keep the rumble of appliances away from the living space. The kitchen space spills into a sunroom which really brings the well landscaped gardens into the home and is a perfect place to relax and read the paper away from the busier parts of the home. Any good home needs lots of nooks and crannies to escape to and here you have them in spades. The living room boasts 22’ x 13’ of living space with a beautiful hardwood fireplace befitting of a country house hotel. There is a large south-west facing seated bay window with a cosy window seat to sit and watch the world go by. This is a room where you will fit most of your furniture making it a real home from home. Just off the utility room a staircase leads to the second floor. Upstairs, things are somewhat more contemporary with the conversion being done in more recent times. There are two large double bedrooms with Velux style windows. One of the bedrooms has been previously used to run a business and the potential for contained office space is phenomenal. The upstairs would work wonderfully well for occasional visitors offering them a level of independence not found in most homes with separate bathroom facilities, potential for a kitchenette whilst being quietly tucked away from the main house. It also benefits from a separate external door entrance if required. Externally there is a large front garden that is south-west facing. The rear garden is very manageable but there is still space for those green fingered buyers amongst you to cultivate and enjoy. There is a useful side garden fit for composting and there are secure double gates leading down each side of the property. The gates are a particular feature of the house and the masonry around them is rather special indeed. The location is truly hard to beat with excellent access to Leeds and Wakefield. Lofthouse has a semi-rural feel and has excellent transport links. The property is very close to the local gp surgery which we think is a massive added bonus. If you would like to view this amazing home then give me a call today to book your viewing.

'A beautifully presented and most individual period home believed to date back to the early 17th Century. This wonderful Grade ll listed home provides flexible and spacious accommodation throughout and extends to approximately 7200 sqft whist retaining much of the buildings original character and charm. A unique and individual opportunity to acquire a wonderful Grade ll listed period home. Thought to have been originally constructed circa 1755 by John Carr for Edwin Lascelles, 1st Lord of Harewood to emulate Harewood House which can be seen from within the main residence. The property offers the potential to further enhance and extend and benefits from planning approval which includes part conversion of the adjoining barn to form an independent guest annex. On approaching this picturesque family home, the discerning purchaser is first drawn to a solid timber door which is set within dressed stone creating a magnificent first impression. An impressive entrance hallway awaits which features a central stone fireplace, matching flank stone archways and parquet flooring, whilst providing access to a vaulted wine cellar. From the entrance hallway, access is then gain to the property’s principal accommodation. The discerning purchaser is then led into a large drawing room which enjoys spectacular views across open countryside and features an open fireplace. Double doors open through into a separate dining room which offers full height vaulted ceilings which presents exposed beams and trusses. Once again, this impressive rooms enjoys far reaching countryside views and provides internal access to the adjoining barn. At the centre of this family home sits a farmhouse style breakfast kitchen which offers a range of solid wall and base units, exposed timber ceiling beams and oil-fired Aga which is set within a tiled recess. The breakfast kitchen in turn leads to the breakfast area off whereby access is then gained to the useful utility room. Further ground floor accommodation includes a guest WC, alongside a separate family room which again displays exposed timber beams and fireplace. Stairs from the entrance hallway lead to the first-floor galleried landing which provides access to all the first floor accommodation. The master suite features exposed ceiling beams and enjoys open countryside views towards Harewood House, whilst being serviced by a recently appointed en-suite bathroom and fully fitted wardrobes. There are two additional double bedrooms at this level and a recently appointed house bathroom. Stairs from the first-floor landing lead to the second floor which offers an additional two bedrooms – one of which benefits from stunning views towards Harewood House. Adjoining the principal dwelling and with internal access from a large boot room which is access via the separate dining room, is a converted two storey stone barn. Comprising of a large pool room which features two fully glazed archways, adjacent changing room, washroom and plant room. Stairs from the ground floor provide access to two first floor rooms which offer the potential for further development (subject to the necessary permissions). Set within approximately six acres, the grounds of this home are approached via a set of electrically operated wrought iron gates which reveals a private driveway that leads to both the front of the property and the rear courtyard which when combined, provide parking for several vehicles. The gardens of this wonderful home are well enclosed and beautifully tended, providing many mature plants and trees. Additionally, the property offers extensive grassed areas which adjoin fenced paddocks and countryside beyond. Situated within an idyllic semi-rural position approximately one mile to the south of the historic estate village of Harewood and a similar distance to the west of Wike. There is ease of access to a host of excellent local conveniences and most denominations of schools including the acclaimed Gateways school in Harewood and Grammar School at Leeds in Alwoodley, both of which are within a five-minute drive. There is also a good range of sporting facilities including the David Lloyd centre and highly regarded golf courses including Alwoodley and Moortown close by. The property is ideally placed for access to principal Yorkshire centres including those of Leeds, Harrogate and the market town of Wetherby. Leeds/Bradford International Airport is also within some 20 minutes’ drive.

'
