Bedroom 1 is a sizeable double room, with fitted wardrobes, situated next to the bathroom- which itself has well chosen tiling by the gloss white shower over bath, a WC and separate wash basin. The second bedroom suits a guest suite, allowing for a double bed too. The modern fitted kitchen, with space for a fridge freezer and washing machine, also has an external door- providing access from the side of the property. Externally the ground floor apartment has a driveway and lovely south west facing rear patio too. Well located to take advantage of all that Brockholes has to offer, as well as the wider Holme Valley, such as an excellent local primary school, a village store, regular bus services and close proximity to the train station which connects Huddersfield to Sheffield. The home could behave as a base for those purchasers looking for something with the ability to “lock up and leave”. The property has gas central heating, provided by high efficiency Gas Condensing Boiler with Hive Active Heating allowing operation of system when away from home, and double glazing throughout. The essentials: The property is leasehold, with a 999 year lease from 18 September 2000, on a "peppercorn" rent. Mains services are connected. The property is Council Tax band A (Kirklees mbc)'

text_description: Lee Royd is located on Heptonstall Road, less than a five-minute walk from the centre of Hebden Bridge, renowned for its vibrant community and independent cafes, shops, bars & restaurants. Backing onto mature oak woodland, this delightful home offers the best of both worlds; for commuters the railway station is just 15 minutes walk or a short bus ride away, while footpaths from the doorstep head up through the woods towards Heptonstall and wonderful moorland beyond. There's a short set of steps up to the front terrace, meaning the living accommodation is nicely set back and elevated above the road, further enhancing the gorgeous views from every room. While the house itself is enormously appealing, the real jewel in the crown here is the delightful rear garden. Set over several terraces rising behind the house it's a very good size, enjoying great privacy and wonderful views over the rooftops to stunning Yorkshire countryside. The front door opens into a small lobby area, a practical space to hang coats and stash your boots after a muddy walk. An inner door leads into a large open-plan living space which takes up the entire ground floor. You'll immediately be struck by how light and bright the room is - being south facing it enjoys sunshine throughout the day and the large window has a great view out over trees towards Hebden Bridge. But the main feature in here is the stunning Yorkshire stone fireplace, housing a woodburning stove perfect for the cooler autumn evenings. After a long day simply light the stove, put your feet up and relax with a box set and hard-earned drink. What could be better? To the rear of the room is the kitchen, with oak-topped units laid out in a generous U shape. There's plenty of space to cook as a family, with a 1.5-bowl sink, built in gas hob and double electric oven, plus room for a fridge, freezer and dishwasher. Alongside there's space for the dining table, making this a very practical and social layout, whether you're keeping an eye on the kids while you cook, or having friends over for food. Moving upstairs, there's two bedrooms and the family bathroom on the first floor, all very well presented. Bedroom two is a good-sized double, with bespoke built in wardrobe and shelving to either side of the chimney breast. Vibrantly decorated, it's a very light and welcoming room, enjoying superb views. Next door, bedroom three is also a double, this time to the rear of the house and overlooking the garden. A sound-insulated cupboard houses a new combination boiler, supplying heating and hot water to the house. Finally on this floor the family bathroom is very tranquil, bathed in light and with original floorboards underfoot. Tastefully decorated in pale blue, there's a large twin-ended bath with shower over, offering the choice of an invigorating shower or, when you have more time, a relaxing soak. Finally, on the top floor there's an excellent master bedroom with ensuite shower room, plus a useful study room, each brightly lit thanks to three large roof windows. The door from the stairs opens into the main bedroom, which has exposed purlins adding character and excellent headroom. This is a large double room, with plenty of space for the bed and creative bespoke joinery. Just off this room is a good-sized ensuite shower room which also has space for the washing machine and tumble dryer. Finally, a door opens from the bedroom into a cosy office space with fitted shelving tucked under the eaves. This an ideal escape for finding peace and quiet when working from home, or how about creating a large walk-in wardrobe? But now back to the wonderful outside space, which is so hard to find in such a central location. To the front of the house, raised above Heptonstall Road there's a small terrace directly outside the front door. With space for a few pots plus a table and chairs it's a real suntrap, and the ideal spot for a morning cuppa. Meanwhile the back garden is truly idyllic, with woodland to the rear and enjoying stunning views and sunshine for most of the day. Divided into three main terraces linked by a wandering path it has a magical, hidden-away feel. There are zones laid out for eating al-fresco, enjoying a sun-down beer or simply relaxing in the sunshine, each with high levels of privacy thanks to thoughtful planting. If growing your own veg appeals there are raised beds too. Right in the middle is a large workshop with power, perfect for raising young plants or for use as a hobby room. Alternatively this would make a great spot for a summerhouse or garden office. A few further basics: There's plenty of on-street parking close to the house. All windows are UPVC double-glazed and heating and hot water is provided by a new combination boiler. In addition to the garden workshop there are two very useful stone sheds under the front terrace, one used for storing the bins and the other as secure bicycle storage. So, to summarise, this is a lovely, good-sized home with a flexible layout. Suitable for a couple or family, it has a wonderful location on the edge of Hebden Bridge within a stone's throw of town and wonderful countryside. With stunning views from every room this isn't a property to miss. So call now, 24/7, to ask any questions and book your place to view on our open day, Saturday 7th January. Inglefield is a striking and unique period family home. Nestled within private landscaped gardens and your own private wood, this superb family home boasts panoramic and unspoilt views over open countryside. Inglefield is perfectly placed to 'get away from it all', as it is for the commuter. Perfectly placed terraces are situated to the front of the property to follow the sun and admire the breath taking views. Location description Inglefield is situated within the 'Golden Triangle' in the premium south side village of Kirkby Overblow; with its own renowned primary school, church and public house. There is a good-sized living room area, big enough to incorporate a table and chairs with space to spare. The kitchen area is beautifully appointed and has lots of hidden extras. Proceeding straight on from the hallway will take you into the double bedroom, which has fitted wardrobes and floor-to-ceiling windows. Not to be outdone, the bathroom has a contemporary white suite, with a waterfall shower over the bath and tasteful complementary wall tiling. The high ceilings throughout add to the feel of good natural light and spaciousness. The car parking is situated at the back of the Chapel, within the communal grounds. Visitor car parking too. Aahhh, but what about the amenities, I hear you ask? Well, these will not disappoint either. Horsforth continues to be a popular and sought-after location, due to an abundance of these, which are improving and growing, month by month, year upon year. text_description: 'Introducing the stunning Cromwell House, a character property in a highly sought after location. A spacious plot with fantastic enclosed gardens and courtyard. Comprising five large double bedrooms, multiple reception rooms, four bathrooms and large utility cellar. This is is a property full of charm which you have to see to appreciate all its wonderful potential. Speak to us 24/7 to express your interest and book your viewing. This beautiful stone property dates back to the late 1800\'s and still holds so much of its original charm. The property is ideal for those with a growing family and for those that love to entertain. This home is extremely social and many great days can be had hosting BBQ\'s out on the terrace or hosting cosy winter nights in with a glass of wine, great friends and an open fire. Depending on your requirements the addition of the converted barn to a stunning Annexe opens up a ton of potential for you to consider. Whether it be converting the space into separate living quarters to be rented out privately or even to AirBnB for extra income there is plenty of room for many layouts. Maybe you have older relatives that require their own space but need to be close by, maybe you just want to keep those teenagers at a distance? No problem, this will tick all those boxes. Arriving at Cromwell House, you gain access from Tithe Barn Street and enter through large electric gates. The courtyard is finished with cobblestones and provides parking comfortably for 5 cars. There are flower beds around the outside, a large antique lamp post and plenty of outside power sockets when required. You enter the property into a large entrance hall through a panel door with stained-glass window surround. Immediately you get the feel for this home with large skirting boards, high ceilings and picture rails. To your right you enter the heart of the home, the kitchen/dining/living area. The kitchen is fully fitted with a mixture of wall and base units, a fireplace recess housing a fully working double gas Aga, a marble island with breakfast bar, with integrated electric oven, induction hob and fridges. The kitchen units are finished in a shaker style in a mushroom grey colour and the worktop is solid wood. All of this space is finished with solid wood herringbone flooring. A generous dining area separates the kitchen and living area. The living room continues the theme of the house with decorative coving, ceiling rose and a period fireplace in a marble surround and mantle over with working open fire. Finished beautifully with a full length bay sash window letting in an abundance of light. This is a space where all the family can be together and it provides so much room for entertaining. Across the hall is the formal living room which has plenty of room for a large furniture suite. The large sash windows provide a lovely outlook over the garden. The charming features continue with large decorative coving and picture rail. The room is completed with a decorative fire surround and fireplace. There is a W.C on the ground floor, which is fully tiled and has a white suite. There are several storage cupboards available. Upstairs to the first floor of the main house you head up the grand staircase with hand carved spindles and handrail to be greeted by a spacious landing with access to all bedrooms. Bedroom 1 is a glorious master bedroom residing to the front, right aspect of the property. This room shows off large sash windows, fitted wardrobes with a hidden TV and access to a large ensuite. The ensuite is finished with Amitco flooring, velux windows and built-in storage. There is a large his and hers marble sink unit, shower cubicle and W.C. Across the hall is bedroom 2, a double room with decorative fireplace and decorative coving. This bedroom has exposed wood flooring in a dark varnish. This bedroom has its own ensuite which is tiled throughout with a W.C, stylish wash basin and walk in shower cubicle. The final bedroom in the main house is bedroom 3, just as substantial as the other two and comprising fitted wardrobes; this room has ample storage and overlooks the cobblestone yard. The family bathroom houses a large bath, separate shower cubicle, wash basin and W.C with a large frosted window. This is the perfect spot to relax after a long day with a great book and a glass of your favourite wine. Downstairs you will find a highly versatile utility cellar, the main area contains storage cupboards, worktop space, Belfast sink and plumbing for your washing machine. There is also housing for a tumble dryer. Tucked behind is a separate wine cellar and additional storage rooms. Moving over to the converted barn which now forms a beautiful Annexe this provides a great value to this property. On entering you find a full height glass panelled window with skylights which let in ample natural light, there are also french doors which lead you out to the garden. The current owners use this space as a gym/games room however the function of the room is fully adaptable for your requirements. The current owners did explore the possibility of turning this space into a kitchen/dining area to make the Annexe a standalone functioning property of its own. Carrying on through you enter the living quarters of the Annexe. Currently used as an office but enough room for multiple sofas if you chose to change its purpose. Dating from the early 1800s, Grade II Listed Machpelah was once a Fustian cutter's workshop. Mullioned windows span two full walls, meaning soft light streams in throughout the day, creating a wonderful feel inside the property and providing iconic Hebden Bridge views. If you don't draw or paint already this is the kind of house to inspire you! Exposed Yorkshire stone and wood beams add further character, and the whole property has been recently and sympathetically refurbished. It's something special. Don't let the position on the main road put you off - being on the 2nd and 3rd floors the house is surprisingly quiet, and you couldn't be better placed for everything Hebden Bridge has to offer; the wide range of independent cafes, shops, bars and restaurants are just a short stroll from the door, while the railway station is less than 5 minutes away. From here there are excellent links to Leeds, Manchester and stations beyond, making this the perfect property if you'd like to finally ditch the car. The rear of the building is another world; a fascinating tumble of rooflines, passageways and stone steps hark back to another era. Gardens are set out as terraces built into the hillside over several levels, with the highest one coming with the property. It's quite a climb, but the stunning views are more than worth the effort. It's very private up here and, looking out over the rooftops across the valley, it enjoys the sun all day long. Back to the house, you'll find the entrance up a flight of steps to the left of the building. The door opens into an enormous living space nearly 13 metres long. Mullioned windows set in stone surrounds stretch the full length of the room, filling the space with light. Original wooden beams and exposed stone are beautifully complimented with pale blue paintwork and wood effect flooring, emphasising the space and creating a relaxing feel. The kitchen is to the left, with windows on two sides giving lovely views out over the rooftops and gardens to the rear. Recently refitted, the units are a sophisticated matt blue/grey colour with contrasting wood effect worktops. A breakfast bar separates the kitchen from the dining area, and there's space for a large table making it perfect for family and friends to gather over food. Alongside here is the living area, with plenty of room for a couple of sofas around the woodburning stove. Winter evenings will be a real treat here, cosy around the fire with your favourite tipple and a movie. As if all that wasn't enough there's also a built-in window-seat to the front, perfect for relaxing with a cuppa in the sunshine and soaking in gorgeous views over the canal and park to the hillside opposite. From the rear of the room a spiral staircase ascends to the floor above, emerging into a large landing area which can easily double as a good office space. Open to the eaves and with windows all along one wall there's a great sense of space. Be warned though - the iconic views of Hebden Bridge might distract you from getting much work done! Just off here is bedroom one, with an exposed stone wall, more mullioned windows, beams, wood flooring and striking green and white décor. This is a very large double bedroom, with a relaxing feel and space for the largest of beds. Double doors open into a further large storage space in the eaves. Just across the landing is the house bathroom, which is again very light and spacious. There's windows all along two sides, and a large bath with shower, basin, WC and bidet. The perfect place for a relaxing Sunday soak with the papers! Back downstairs, and a door leads from the open plan living area into a generous hallway, with two more bedrooms and the attic room accessed from here. Bedroom two is to the front of the house and is simply huge! There's a very light and bright feel throughout thanks to light flooding in through the double sash window, which again has great views. An exposed stone wall and original fireplace provide further character, and the room has been designed to allow the addition of a second bathroom if required, without compromising on space. Next door, to the rear of the house is bedroom three, which is another double. Featuring mullioned windows giving a pretty view out onto the terraced gardens behind the building. Finally, a second spiral staircase gives access to a very large loft room, which has excellent headroom throughout. Currently used as a gym / art studio, it's another room with great character and provides flexible space suitable for multiple uses. Perhaps you'd like further office space, a second sitting area / occasional bedroom, or a hobby room? The choice is yours and, brimming with character features again, it's sure to become one of your favourite rooms. So, to recap, this amazing property is all about light and space. With three large bedrooms, the loft room and generous landing space, it's far, far bigger than you might imagine. Recently renovated and tastefully decorated it has a great feel, and also has the bonus of the garden space too. But, most importantly, there's just something special about this house it's hard to put your finger on. To find out more give our friendly team a ring today, 24/7, and book your place to view. We're looking forward to showing you around! Additional Information: Council Tax: Band B Marketed by EweMove Sales & Lettings (Hebden Bridge) - Property Reference 49226

text_description: '\'Satis Cottage\' dating from c.1820 is a most charming, immaculately maintained, two double bedroom, double fronted cottage in the heart of Burley in Wharfedale with off street parking, convenient downstairs W/C and delightful, landscaped, south facing, lawned garden. A half glazed door with attractive decorative glazed panels leads into the spacious lounge. A gas stove set in a stone hearth with exposed brickwork is a fabulous focal feature to this large room. Burley in Wharfedale is a very popular and thriving village community in the heart of the Wharfe Valley, providing a good range of local shops including a Coop local store, doctors’ surgery, library, two excellent primary schools, various inns and restaurants, churches of several denominations and a variety of sporting and recreational facilities. A commuter rail service to Leeds/Bradford city centres, with commuting times of under 30 minutes and Ilkley in 5 minutes, is also available from the village station, only a few minutes\' walk away. This house is ideal for anybody wanting to be close to the vibrant village centre. With gas fired central heating and timber framed double glazing and approximate room sizes the property comprises: Ground Floor Entrance Porch A brand new, solid wood, half glazed door opens into a light and airy entrance porch courtesy of double glazed windows to all sides. Beautiful marble floor tiling, exposed, painted stonework. This is a great spot to sit and enjoy the vista over the lovely front garden and to kick off shoes and boots after a long walk in the surrounding Wharfe Valley countryside. A solid oak door opens to a most useful cloakroom. text_description: Beautiful character barn conversion in the most idyllic location! Dating back to the mid 18th Century is this Grade II Listed barn conversion in the sought after hamlet of Brunthwaite, Silsden. The property has recently undergone major renovations by local builder Enoch Harrison & Sons, and now boasts an impeccable finish throughout with a beautiful contrast between old and new. Internally this one of a kind, family home comprises flexible open plan living with multiple reception rooms, a contemporary fully fitted kitchen and separate utility and a home office/fourth bedroom, benefitting from polished concrete flooring with underfloor heating and is naturally lit via the bespoke double height window situated in the converted original barn entrance on the ground floor. The first floor provides a beautiful galleried landing with high ceilings and restored oak fishbone king-post roof, original exposed beams, three double bedrooms and a family bathroom with the principal bedroom having access to a dressing room, en-suite shower room and mezzanine storage. Externally the property has off-street parking provided by re-laid cobbles to the front. The barn also boasts a four-tier garden to the rear extending to a third of an acre, including a sheltered courtyard, perfect for private outside dining in the summer, leading to a raised cottage garden with a stone patio, perfect for entertaining in the summer sun, then on top a separate walled vegetable garden which leads out to a level open field. Situated 1 mile from the centre of Silsden, Brunthwaite is a historical rural hamlet, full of charm and hidden away off the beaten track. Brunthwaite is surrounded by a network of footpaths offering doorstep access to local moor and woodland. Silsden is a popular and thriving village with excellent local facilities including village shops, supermarket, two primary schools, churches, public houses and eateries. Situated midway between Skipton, Ilkley and Keighley it is an ideal base for the Aire Valley commuter with Steeton & Silsden railway station nearby, offering regular services to Skipton and Bradford/Leeds, with connecting trains through to London Kings Cross. Accommodation Ground Floor Covered Entrance To the front of the property is a covered entrance leading to the front door with original stone flooring and wooden bin store. Lobby The lobby provides a warm welcome to the barn with an oak window seat and built in cloaks cupboard and gives access to the kitchen and downstairs cloakroom. Cloakroom / Utility Downstairs cloakroom and utility comprising an integral washing machine, quartz sink and drainer and a w.c. Kitchen A contemporary fully fitted kitchen with Botticino marble work surfaces and a mixture of handle-less wall and base units. The kitchen also comprises an array of integral AEG appliances including fridge freezer, induction hob with hidden extractor over, twin steam ovens and dishwasher. The island in the kitchen provides further base storage units with marbles surfaces over with a one and a half stainless steel gold sink, and matching mixer tap. Sun Room To the rear of the barn is the second reception room naturally lit by two Velux windows and a large sliding patio door giving access to the courtyard. Living Room A generously proportioned living room with original features such as exposed stone walls, an Inglenook fireplace with contemporary log burning stove and triple aspect windows to front, side and rear. The living room also comprises a feature dining space in front of the double height converted barn entrance and gives access to the first floor via a bespoke solid ash staircase with glass balustrade. First Floor Galleried Landing The galleried landing provides a beautiful open aspect to the first floor with exposed full height original restored beams, engineered oak wood flooring and steel column radiators. The space is flooding with natural light via glazed panels between the beams. Principal Bedroom The main double bedroom is generous in size with an exposed stone wall and Velux windows. A view of Brunthwaite can be seen via an original bird hole window. This bedroom also has access to a dressing room with build in wardrobes, an en-suite shower room and has a steel column radiator. En-Suite A modern en-suite shower room with walk-in shower, hand wash basin with vanity unit, w.c. And radiator. Bedroom Two A second double bedroom comprising Velux windows, a separate window to the covered entrance, an exposed stone wall and steel column radiators. Bedroom Three To the rear is the third double bedroom with steel column radiator and Velux windows. Family Bathroom A modern family bathroom with a four piece suite consisting of a double-ended steel bath, walk-in shower, hand wash basin with vanity and w.c. The bathroom also comprises built in oak shelving and an exposed stone wall. External To the front of the barn is off-street parking on re-laid original cobbles providing space for two cars to park. The rear garden stretches to around a third of an acre accessed via the sun room and living room and boasts a sheltered courtyard with re-layed Herringbone brick, a raised cottage garden with Yorkshire stone patio, a stone walled vegetable garden with garden shed and greenhouse giving access to a level open field with large shed and unrivalled views to the far edge of Ilkley Moor. Tenure We have been advised that the property is freehold. Viewing Arrangements We would be pleased to arrange a viewing for you. Please contact Dale Eddison's Skipton office. Our opening hours are:- Monday to Friday: 9.00am - 5.30pm Saturday: 9.00am - 4.00pm Sunday: 11.00am - 3.00pm Directions From Skipton proceed on the A629 (Aire Valley Bypass) in the direction of Keighley and after around 6 miles turn left into Silsden village. In the centre of the village turn right onto Clog Bridge which turns into Howden Road. At the top of Howden Road, turn left onto Hawber Lane and then first right onto Brunthwaite Lane. The property is located on the left hand side.

Local Area Cleckheaton sits in the borough of Kirklees, in the historic region of Yorkshire's West Riding. The town stands at the centre of The Spen Valley: An area which grew prosperous in the 19th century, through an abundance of Victorian industry. Today the Spen Valley is far more sedate, and the old lines of the freight railways have been replaced by the scenic cycling routes of the Spen Valley Greenway. Cleckheaton's own former industrial wealth can still be seen in its grand churches and elegant civic halls, and the town still remains a bustling profusion of handsome stone-fronted Victorian buildings. Cleckheaton has a friendly and welcoming community feel, and the town is well-served by a host of amenities and services, including doctors; pharmacies and high street banks - not to mention a fantastic selection of shops; supermarkets; and specialist local businesses - all within easy reach. Sporting enthusiasts will find a friendly welcome at the Cleckheaton & District Golf Club and the town also has a sports club and two bowling greens. Cleckheaton has a varied and highly-recommended selection of pubs and restaurants, along with plenty of cafes, coffee shops and takeaways. On the first Saturday of every month, Cleckheaton holds a popular Farmers' Market, offering a mouth-watering array of delicious seasonal produce. There's also the annual Cleckheaton Folk Festival, providing live music, street entertainment and craft events. Cleckheaton is served by a modern bus station and is well situated for motorway access. text_description: A three bedroom, semi detached family home enjoying a good size corner plot in a most convenient position only a short walk from the train station and village amenities. This is a fabulous opportunity to acquire a modern, three bedroom, semi detached house set on a generous corner plot in the centre of this popular Wharfedale village. Offering potential to further extend (subject to planning) the house has been remodelled on the ground floor to provide a contemporary open plan dining kitchen with French doors leading out to the rear garden. The kitchen offers a range of modern units complimented by contrasting 'granite effect' work surfaces and a range of integrated appliances. A generously proportioned lounge with a living flame electric fire completes the ground floor. On the first floor there are two double bedrooms and a single bedroom, currently in use as a home office, along with a house bathroom and separate WC. There is also access via a loft ladder to a very useful attic which has recently been boarded. As the property is set on a corner plot there are lawned gardens to the front and side with planted borders. To the rear there is driveway parking giving access to the detached garage. The rear garden is mainly paved. Prospect Road forms part of a very popular residential neighbourhood close to the centre of this thriving mid Wharfedale village community. Burley in Wharfedale provides a useful range of local shops, doctors’ surgery, inns, restaurants and churches of several denominations, many of which are readily accessible. There are two primary schools within the village and variety of sporting and recreational facilities including the nearby cricket ground. There are also delightful walks to be enjoyed through the countryside surrounding the village. Indeed, Burley in Wharfedale is considered an ideal location in the Wharfe Valley countryside for commuters to Leeds/Bradford city centres to which regular rail services are available from the village railway station on Station Road. The nearby towns of Ilkley and Otley provide a wider range of facilities less than five miles away. From our office on Station Road proceed in the direction of the Station and take the fifth left turn onto Prospect Road. Follow the road round the sharp right bend and the property will be found just on the left.

There are bus services into the city centre and Wakefield benefits from good rail links. Of the two railway stations, Westgate is on the Leeds to London route, with journey times of less than 15 minutes to Leeds and two hours to London Kings Cross, while Kirkgate serves stations to Sheffield and Nottingham. The city of Wakefield presents a superb choice of cultural and leisure attractions set against a background of fascinating architecture and heritage, including the magnificent Wakefield Cathedral and Sandal Castle. In addition to visual arts at The Hepworth, Yorkshire Sculpture Park and several smaller galleries, the Theatre Royal presents an eclectic programme of drama and music, and the new Unity Works is a vibrant venue for social gatherings and live music. There is an excellent choice of cinemas, bars, restaurants and nightlife, including soul nights at the celebrated Red Bar. Wakefield’s sporting and leisure provision include the superb Pugneys Watersports Centre and Country Park on the southern edge of the city, where there are facilities for sailing, windsurfing and canoeing, and the choice of leisure centres in the area includes Sun Lane Leisure, where there is a 25m swimming pool, a fitness suite and a gym. Other amenities nearby include Normanton Golf Club, around a mile to the north, and Pontefract Racecourse is less than ten miles away. The City Fields proposals include a neighbourhood centre within a short walk of the homes, with a range of shops including food retailers, restaurants, a medical centre and other services. There is also a small local shopping area on Windhill Road with a pharmacist, a post office and a convenience store, while the city centre offers a very wide choice of high street chains, malls and traditional shops. A major recycling centre on Denby Dale Road, three and a half miles away, accepts virtually all household packaging, electrical items and clothing. An area within the wider City Fields neighbourhood, close to Wakefield City Academy, has been set aside for educational provision. However, there is also a choice of established primary schools within walking distance, from where pupils normally move on to either Outwood Grange Academy or St Thomas à Becket rc College for secondary education. There is a large fulltime gp practice at New Southgate Surgery, approximately a mile and a half away, and Pinderfields General Hospital, around half a mile from The Woods, operates a round-the- clock A&E department. If you would prefer to, you can still make an appointment by calling our sales centre or booking on our website. text_description: Set down a private lane is Broad Oak Barn. Presented to an exceptionally high standard but with many original features still incorporated throughout, the property sits within generous gardens which has several ponds, fruit trees and a stone patio area with privacy all round. This barn conversion has 4 bedrooms, plus home office/bedroom 5, double garage and parking and an open plan kitchen/dining room. Broad Oak Barn is set within the popular area of Colne Valley with many local amenities near by. As you approach the property located down the private lane, you are immediately drawn to the uniqueness of the barn with the original stone stairs at the front leading up to the first floor bedroom and the lavishly elegant flower beds by the entrance. To the left of the property is the large driveway, big enough told hold up to 6 cars, and then the double garage located at the bottom. At the end of the lane, there is also a turning circle where there is an allocated parking space for this property. Currently used as a games room, the garage has an up and over door to the front, and an access door to the side. There is a greenhouse attached to the side of the garage, perfect for growing your own fruit and vegetables. Upon entrance to Broad Oak Barn, the hallway is the perfect space for removing outdoor garments before leading into the kitchen/dining room. A downstairs W.C is located in the hallway with laminate flooring, wash basin and close coupled W.C. With ceramic tiled flooring flowing throughout the kitchen and dining room, this is the perfect space for entertaining guests and sitting down at a large dining table with the family for dinner. The kitchen consists of solid oak cupboards and granite worktops, Falcon integrated cooker with overhead cooker hood, integrated dishwasher and double Belfast sink. To the right of the kitchen through the partitioned doors is the sitting room. With solid oak flooring and a stone fireplace with remote controlled stove, the room still holds some of the original features of the property, but with the modernisation of the neutral décor gives a very ambient feel for a family to cosy up in front of the fire. Bifold doors in this room lead you out into the rear gardens, filling the room with natural light. Set to the left of the property is a very spacious utility room with solid oak cupboards and granite effect tops. This space holds the boiler and has plumbing for a washing machine and dryer and also includes a sink. The stairs that lead to the first floor are located in the dining room where you are met with a generous sized landing space which incorporates the original beams and high ceilings. There are 3 double bedrooms situated on this floor, 2 of which have en-suites with ceramic tiled flooring, wash basin, shower and W.C. The en-suites also have electric Velux windows which enhances natural light and brightens crisp white furnishings. On this floor, there is also the house bathroom. With a 3 piece Fordham suite consisting of wash basin, shower and W.C, the room adds a modern feel to the property with the ceramic tiled flooring and large fitted mirror perfect for winding down after a hard day at work. All the bedrooms are neutrally decorated to fit everyone's needs. The master bedroom and one other double room overlooks the cricket field providing plenty of light and a scenic view. A further room on this floor is used as a dressing room, with fitted wardrobes and laminate flooring, this can easily be adapted if needed into a 4th bedroom or home office. To the rear of the property sits the amazing professionally landscaped gardens extending to 0.25 acre approx. text_description: Description Norwood House dates back to the early 1890's and is a beautiful four bedroom, double fronted Victorian terrace in the heart of Morley. The huge rooms, lovely period features and additional outbuilding with all manner of options for use, making this a truly unique home. Close to Morley town centre with bars, restaurants, supermarket, shops and transport links just a stones throw away, Westfield Road is a sought after location. Popular primary and secondary schools are a short walk away with doctor and dental surgeries on your doorstep. Commuting to Leeds or Wakefield couldn't be easier with bus and train stations nearby and motorway links a few minutes drive away for those travelling further afield. Step inside... Arriving on Westfield Road, Norwood house stands out with its attractive double frontage and traditional iron railings surrounding the front garden. Step through the smart front door into the entrance vestibule with doors leading to the two front reception rooms and stairs rising to the first floor. Here you'll get your first glimpse of the beautful period detail on the cornice and mouldings. Lounge To the left of the main entrance is the lounge. Recently decorated this magnificent reception room is of grand proportions and has a beautiful ornate ceiling with the original ceiling rose and cornice which show off the rich heritage of this home. A more recent fireplace is the focal point of the room with a window looking out to the front. A lovely room to entertain guests or relax on an evening in front of the fire with a glass of wine. Sitting Room Also at the front of the house is the sitting room. Currently used as a day lounge this room would also work well as a formal dining room being next door to the kitchen. Another feature fireplace is the focal point of the room and window overlooks the front garden. There is also access to the cellar here which is a useful storage space with two rooms. Kitchen/Diner Next door is the recently fitted kitchen with space for a dining table. Heritage colours on the shaker style cabinets and walls are complimented by the solid wood work surfaces which provide plenty of preparation space. A stainless steel integrated oven, ceramic hob with extractor over and integrated fridge freezer plus space for a washing machine. Window to the rear and side overlook the garden and patio area and an entrance door leads out onto the sunny patio - perfect for a summer BBQ. You can just imagine a leisurely Sunday morning breakfast at the table whilst reading the paper or chat with your partner as one of you makes dinner and the other sits and relaxes. Landling Heading back through the sitting room and into the hallway and take the stairs to the first floor. The spacious landing has a window overlooking the rear garden and access to the bedrooms and bathroom and loft access. Master Bedroom Directly above the lounge, the Master Bedroom enjoys the same vast proportions and makes a grand retreat from a busy day. The room has neutral décor and a beautiful original fireplace and could easily accommodate large pieces of bedroom furniture and maybe even add an ensuite, without ever feeling cramped. You might also consider converting bedroom four next door into an ensuite bathroom to make an impressive master suite. Bedroom Two To the rear of the house is the second bedroom, a lovely sunny room with windows to the rear and side and another large double bedroom. This could make a lovely guest room or for children there's plenty of space for bunk beds and till leave lots of room to play. Bedroom Three To the front of the house is the third bedroom, a further double bedroom which would be great as a child's bedroom and would make a lovely nursery. Bedroom Four Currently used as a single bedroom, this space would work very well as a home office or study. Bathroom Fully tiled, the modern bathroom has a tasteful décor and a white three piece bathroom suite with bath with shower over, hand basin and WC. Light a candle and run a luxurious bubble bath and relax and unwind after a busy day. Step outside... The front of the house has a low maintenance paved garden. To the side of the house is a private driveway which leads to the rear garden / yard and workshop. The fully enclosed rear garden is fully paved and again low maintenance. There is a patio area just outside the kitchen door which is south facing so enjoys sun all day, perfect for a BBQ or sitting with a morning coffee. To the rear of the yard is a large two storey brick built workshop. This interesting building is full of history and has a stable and two garages on the ground floor with a very large workshop area and office to the first floor. This has so much potential and could possibly be converted to separate living accommodation and would be large enough for two dwellings subject to planning approval. It could also be ideal for someone looking to combine business premises with their home. Or you might just want to use it as garages and storage which would also work. The yard in front of the workshop has plenty of space to park multiple vehicles and there is a gate providing vehicle access to the side. Finer details... Fully double glazed with doors and windows having been replaced within the last couple of years. Gas central heating throughout Leeds city council Council tax band A EPC rating E Council Tax Band: A Tenure: Freehold

text_description: 'Located on the main street in the historic village of Heptonstall, this unique character property is a rare find. This is an exceptional property with an intriguing layout that enhances the space and light throughout the property. This Grade II residence offers superb flexible living space. If you are looking for something a little different this property firmly ticks that box.. Your eyes can\'t help but be drawn to the multitude of quirky and interesting features of this property. As you walk around the place there are lovely little touches that will bring a smile to your face, be that the open tread staircases, the beautiful floors or the hidden \x91Minecraft style\' den suspended above one of the bedrooms. Let\'s have a tour around this versatile and welcoming property which offers many a hidden gem... As you enter this home there is a small porch area that provides protection from the worst of the elements and is ideal for muddy boots or paws. Then on entering the main living space you will catch your first glimpse of the split level open plan living space which characterises this stunning property. The first living space is currently used as a dining room, the lovely stone fireplace sets the scene and offers a warm welcome. The room has ample space for a large dining table which would lend itself perfectly to formal dining or gatherings with the whole family present. A few steps up and you can enjoy further comfort in the lounge, it is a good sized room with beautifully retained features which are echoed throughout the entire property. This unique living space is bursting with character, mullion windows span the width of the room and cast a wonderful light and a charming window seat is where you will spend many an hour gazing out across the valley. It is a generous room with ample space for a chunky sofa, perfect for cosy evenings in with the latest box set. Steps lead down from the dining room into the kitchen which is a perfect balance of traditional features and contemporary design .It is a well equipped kitchen with ample storage and sufficient worktops, if you\'re serious about cooking this kitchen will certainly work for you. The large pantry is a very welcome addition here. The kitchen leads to a large storage room with plumbing for a washing machine and space for a dryer. A stunning internal stained glass window greets you with a ground floor bathroom beyond this. A door leads to the rear garden area from the kitchen. The living space on the ground floor is further enhanced by a multi use room, accessed from the dining room currently used as a home office by the present owner. There is a door leading to the front of the property which further enhances the practicality of this room. Heading up the open tread staircase, there are three double bedrooms with one enjoying a mezzanine level accessed by a ladder in the corner of the room. The bathroom is situated on the top landing and comprises a 4 piece suite in white with wall mounted w/c with recessed flush, next to this is another large storage room which spans the full width of the house, add to this extra loft space and all your storage needs are answered. To the rear of the property the paved garden terrace is the ideal spot to sit with your favourite tipple taking in the far reaching views. The property has gas central heating and double glazing which makes for a beautifully warm home with a lovely welcoming feel, with neutral decor throughout it is ready to move straight in. The location of this property is very appealing, situated in the very heart of Heptonstall on the main street with stunning valley views to the rear. This conservation village with its iconic churchyard has local amenities in easy reach, including a couple of pubs, the post office and primary school. You are just a short distance away from the range of independent retailers, bars and restaurants in Hebden Bridge and Todmorden. How fantastic would it be to live in this village location? It is a lovely place to be, close to open countryside where you can walk the dog or take a jog along the many leafy footpaths. There is also a greenhouse with power laid on, raised vegetable beds, fruit trees and external water supply. text_description: Barkers Terrace is an impressive building located in the Conservation Area on Hangingroyd Road, right in the heart of Hebden Bridge. You couldn't be better placed for everything this funky Bohemian town has to offer; the wide range of independent cafes, shops, bars and restaurants are just a short stroll from the front door, while the railway station is a mere 10 minutes walk away. From here there are excellent links to Leeds, Manchester and stations beyond, so if you're looking for an opportunity to go car-free this is it! Being so centrally placed the property is also ideal for rental purposes and the present owner has made a good income this way in the past. It's also worth noting straight away that the property has never been flooded during the owner's 20 years in the house. Number five has an angled front wall, giving rooms on this side of the building an interesting, quirky feel - very Hebden Bridge! The front door opens into a small tiled lobby area, with room to hang coats and access to a useful large storage cupboard under the stairs. Just to the right is the very welcoming living room. This is a wonderful family space, drenched in light from the enormous sash windows. There's high ceilings, deep coving and a beautiful ceiling rose, all adding character. With plenty of room for two large sofas it's easy to imagine relaxing here with a movie and, during winter, cosying up around the lovely open fire, another feature original to the house. From the living room it's a single step up into the dining-kitchen, which has more than enough room for a large dining table in front of the woodburning stove - perfect for entertaining over food. The kitchen has lots of storage and workspace for the busy household, a gas hob, electric oven and space for all the usual appliances. There's a large window to the rear with borrowed light, but it would be a straightforward job to copy the neighbours by knocking through into the living room to create a semi open-plan kitchen / dining / living space, the perfect heart for this spacious home. Heading back into the living room, and the staircase leads up to the first floor, where you'll find the first of three double bedrooms, each similar in size and located on a separate floor. On the first and second floors the bedrooms feature large sash windows, making them very light and bright and offering lovely views, while the top floor is a cosy attic space with a roof window. text_description: Situated on a lovely tree-lined avenue in the heart of residential Roundhay is a deceptively spacious, six bedroom semi-detached property, which has been stylishly yet sympathetically refurbished to offer practical and well-laid-out family living space, with modern comforts married perfectly with period features. The centrally heated accommodation has extensive PVCu double glazing, beautifully proportioned rooms, many of which have particularly high ceilings with cornicing and other features including original stripped panelled internal doors and decorative fireplaces. The internal accommodation includes a lovely large entrance hall with decorative leaded stained glass around the doorway, staircase to the first floor with original decorative balustrading, and access to the basement. There is a light and elegant living room to the front enjoying a double aspect afforded by a circular bay window to the front elevation and additional window to the side, and a focal fireplace in cast iron grate with decorative surround. The sitting/dining room to the rear has been partially opened up to the kitchen creating practical family living space which is also perfect for entertaining, having double French doors set within a high decorative archway affording direct access to the rear garden, and there is a log burner set within the chimney breast recess with a stone lintel and hearth. An open rectangular archway leads to the kitchen area, which has a well-designed layout of low level painted base units and drawers with granite worktop surfaces and splashbacks, and has space for a range style cooker set within the original chimney breast, with decorative stone lintel and overhead filter hood. Double French doors afford a pleasant aspect as well as direct access onto the rear garden, and there is also a useful utility/downstairs WC. To the first floor are two particularly large double bedrooms, a good size third bedroom (which could accommodate a double bed) and the house bathroom which has underfloor heating and is fitted with a modern four piece suite in white including a walk-in shower. To the second floor are two further double bedrooms and a generous sixth bedroom (which could also accommodate a double bed), all with exposed beams, and a bathroom fitted with a three piece white suite. The house stands in an attractive position towards the top of North Park Grove and has a slightly elevated front garden with a central lawn surrounded by mature trees and shrubbery. A driveway affords off-road parking, and a gate provides access round to the rear garden which has a 'U' shaped timber deck across the back of the house, which leads onto a lawn where there is a timber garden storage shed. The rear garden backs onto neighbouring gardens which means that it is not directly overlooked from behind. A stunning family home of character and distinction, genuinely worthy of internal viewing. text_description: Are you looking for a good sized home in the heart of a semi-rural village? A property with some real character, but without compromising on room sizes? text_description: Lee Royd is located on Heptonstall Road, less than a five-minute walk from the centre of Hebden Bridge with its excellent choice of independent cafes, shops, bars and restaurants. The house enjoys lovely valley views in a best-of-both-worlds location backing onto woodland. It's just 15 minutes walk or a short bus ride to the railway station, with regular trains to Leeds, Manchester and beyond making this a great property for commuters. Meanwhile walkers and cyclists will love the easy access to gorgeous Calderdale countryside, with footpaths close to the house heading up towards Heptonstall and the moorland beyond. There's a short set of steps up to the private front terrace which is elevated above Heptonstall Road with great far-reaching views. There's generous space for a table, chairs and some pots and, being south-east facing, this is a real sun-trap and the perfect spot for a morning cuppa or lunch in the sunshine. From the terrace, the front door opens straight into the spacious open-plan reception room. This is a really light and bright space which enjoys sunshine throughout most of the day. You'll immediately pick up on the period details in here, with a gorgeous wood parquet floor, picture rail, exposed brick chimney breast and a stunning Yorkshire stone fireplace. The fireplace houses a large wood-burning stove which supplements the gas central heating and makes for a really cosy feel. Winter's evenings relaxing here with a glass of wine and a book will be a real treat! To the rear of the room is the kitchen, hand-made in pine and forming an L shape to maximise space for a large dining table alongside. The kitchen features a Belfast sink with a range of bespoke cupboards and drawers. There's a good amount of storage plus space for a cooker and washing machine, with the fridge-freezer and dishwasher cleverly tucked close-by beneath the stairs. Being open-plan the downstairs layout is very social, perfect for throwing parties or having friends over for dinner. Up the stairs and the feeling of character continues, with stripped pine doors and exposed wood flooring throughout the first floor. Bedroom two is a good-sized double, with a lovely original Victorian fireplace and space for a wardrobe and shelving to either side. Simply decorated, it's a light and welcoming room, with great views to the front. Next door, bedroom three is also a double, this time to the rear and overlooking the garden. This is a very cosy room, with William Morris Willow Bough wallpaper and more exposed floorboards. Finally on this floor the house bathroom is a good size, light and bright, with stripped wood panelling, a bath with shower over, basin and WC. With a really tranquil feel, it's easy to imagine lazy Sunday mornings spent relaxing in the bath. Bliss! Finally, on the second floor there's an excellent master bedroom taking up the entire top floor of the house. Exposed purlins, wood cladding and another original fireplace make for another characterful room, and shelving and cupboards are built-in under the eaves. With two large roof windows and excellent headroom there's potential to subdivide this space, perhaps to create a fourth bedroom or ensuite shower room. Moving outside, in addition to the front terrace there's an enclosed garden to the rear, accessed from the kitchen via a set of steps. This is the place for sunshine during the afternoon, and the mature planting gives a great degree of privacy. Currently there's a good-sized shed and a small patio area, with the rest of the space laid to lawn, but there's the potential to be creative and make something really special here. A few further basics: There's plenty of on-street parking close to the house. All windows are double-glazed and heating and hot water is provided by a Worcester combination boiler located in a cupboard off the landing. In addition to the garden shed there is a good-sized former coal house under the front terrace. Don't miss out - character homes like this don't hang around for long! In a brilliant location, and with stunning views from every room, call now, 24/7, to ask any questions and book your place to view on our open day, Sunday 8th January. text_description: Located on Burnley Road, the house is set back behind a smart gravelled fore-garden and is handily placed for Mytholmroyd's shops, cafes, pubs, schools and the community centre. Transport links are excellent - it's just a short stroll to the railway station with regular services to Leeds and Manchester, and the bus stop is close-by too. There's also easy access to the cycle path linking Hebden Bridge with Sowerby Bridge, and there are numerous beautiful country walks accessible straight from the door, making this a real best-of-both-worlds location. The house is a handsome brick built semi-detached with a distinctive 1930s square bay window. Inside, it's been sympathetically modernised with quality fittings and neutral decoration, making a great blank canvas. Stepping through the front door there's a small lobby area, perfect for hanging your coat before moving further into the house. A door to the left opens into the living room, with deep coving to the ceiling and an attractive alcove alongside the chimney breast adding a touch of character. There's a cosy gas fire, perfect for snuggling up during the winter months, and a huge bay window making the room beautifully light whatever the weather. A door leads onwards into the breakfast kitchen, which is a very good size. The kitchen has been recently re-fitted to a great standard, with quality Neff oven and ceramic hob built-in. There's a good number of base and wall units, plentiful working space plus room for an American fridge-freezer, dishwasher, washing machine and tumble dryer. In addition there's access to a very large understairs cupboard and a second large cupboard which houses the combination boiler and provides excellent further storage. At one end is a space ideal for a small table, but if you prefer a more formal dining space, how about extending the house to the rear? The patio accessed via the back door from the kitchen is very large and there's easy scope for adding an extension while still maintaining a good sized outdoor space. Upstairs there are two double bedrooms and the bathroom, plus a loft room with ladder access. Starting with bedroom one, this is a very large double room, with plenty of space for a large double bed, plus further bedroom furniture. There's a good-sized wardrobe built in over the stairs too. Next door, bedroom two is a smaller double, but would make a perfect guest bedroom / study or children's room. Finally, the bathroom is modern and brightly lit thanks to the large window. There's a WC, basin and a large bath with shower and glass screen. Things are kept nice and toasty thanks to the heated chrome towel radiator. Finally, a drop down ladder on the landing gives access to a room in the loft. It's a good size with a roof window, power and lighting and although headroom is limited, it provides excellent storage and the potential for use as an occasional hobby room / office. Outside, the large rear patio garden is accessed either from the kitchen or via a side gate from the front. Attractively paved, there's plenty of room for garden furniture and it would be a brilliant spot for an evening BBQ. If gardening appeals there's scope to get creative with some raised beds, or how about a garden office? A few extra practicalities: Parking is available on-street nearby. The house is double glazed throughout and heating is provided by an Ideal gas combination boiler, plus the gas fire in the living room. To summarise, this is a very well-maintained and presented home in a popular location, right on the doorstep of central Mytholmroyd. Room sizes are excellent, with the possibility of extending the kitchen to the rear if you require extra living space. Modestly priced and ticking so many boxes, we're expecting plenty of interest in this lovely property. So don't delay - call now, 24/7, and book your place to view on our open day, Sunday 8th January. text_description: Are you looking for a nice home with great gardens, a lovely outlook and a fabulous view? This semi detached home offers far more than you might notice at first glance. For a start, it's not actually on Keighley Road, but rather overlooks a green space off Whitehill Drive. The good sized accommodation boasts two double bedrooms which some people have divided to create a three bedroomed home, such is the size and flexibility. Fixtures and fittings provide the crossover of modern and traditional, with a lovely wood burning fire stove to go with the gas central heating, the uPVC double glazing, the modern kitchen and shower fitments... However, it's outside that we think a this house really does come into its own. The side garden in particular is a good size, offering a great family space, and extension potential for those looking to the future, subject to the required consents, of course. Positioned as it is, that outlook over a nice open green space sits in front of the far reaching views which can be seen best from the upper floor. With access to local supermarket, schools, and the Halifax town centre quite easy via Keighley Road, this is one you really shouldn't miss. EPC Rating: C Location Leave Halifax along the A629 Keighley Road. Proceed along this road for approximately two miles, passing Morrison's supermarket, and continue on up round the bend. Once the road levels out, turn right into Illingworth Road. Turn right again just before the shops into Moss Drive, and then first right into Whitehill Drive. At the t-junction turn left, where the house will be found overlooking the public open space. Postcode: HX2 9DN. Entrance Hall A welcoming hallway with a window to the side and stairs to the first floor. There is a useful storage cupboard here, too. Through Lounge And Dining Room (6.42m x 3.82m) The central focal point of this good sized living space Is the brick chimney breast and fireplace which houses a wood burner: A great feature which provides that warm glow, particularly in winter. The room narrows a little to 2.73 metres in the dining area, as you can see on the floor plan. Kitchen (2.93m x 2.81m) Fitted with a modern range of grey, high gloss base and wall units with contrasting work surfaces and surrounds. There are integrated cooking appliances including a four burner gas hob and an electric oven, along with a sink unit with a mixer tap. Rear Porch (1.96m x 1.19m) A great place for coats and shoes, but with ample space for a chest freezer, or perhaps an American style fridge. We personally think this would make a great utility room. First Floor Landing With useful cupboards and a frosted window to the side gardens. Bedroom One (4.70m x 3.02m) A good sized double bedroom which has a traditional tiled fireplace and solid grate, purely decorational these days. The outlook from this room is lovely, and those far reaching views can be seen from the windows. There is a useful storage cupboard above the bulkhead, too. Some people within these houses have divided this room in two, making a three bedroomed home, and we can understand why. We really love the size and shape of it now, though. The room extends to 5.75 metres, as shown in the floor plan. Bedroom Two (3.34m x 3.28m) A second good sized double bedroom, this one to the rear, again with a nice aspect which looks along the gardens to the public open space to the back. The open floorboards are just waiting to be sanded and stained or varnished, and you will note from the floor plan that the bedroom widens at the entrance. Shower Room A nice wet room with a walk-in shower and a wash basin. The walls are tiled and there is a useful cabinet over the wash basin, along with a heated tower rail to the drying area. WC With a low flush suite. Garden The gardens here are a real surprise. They are lower maintenance, but provide a great degree of space, either to use or to extend into. The front garden is finished with pebbles and provides a lovely approach. The rear garden is mainly paved, with some flower beds and a useful garden store. The side garden is the real crown jewel of this particular home, providing a large fenced garden for that degree of security, particularly when considering younger children. There's a slightly raised seating area with artificial turf, here, too. There's a summer house and a store to round things off nicely. Of course an extension may require planning consent and would need building regulations approval.

text_description: 'About the aisled barn This unique grade II listed building is originally believed to date back to the 17th century and is attached to a former farmhouse. It enjoys a superb rural setting in the much admired Shibden Valley and is located towards the end of a winding unmade track. It originally formed part of Scout Hall Farm which was within the curtilage of Scout Hall, a noted stately home which was the home of a local silk merchant. The internal accommodation features a large open plan space which incorporates living, dining and kitchen areas with a polished concrete floor and exposed crook frame with the ceiling open to the eaves and double height. The principal bedroom is also located on this floor and is of a good size with large picture windows to the front and rear. There is a large en-suite bathroom off the bedroom. A cantilevered wooden staircase with glazed balustrade leads up to the second floor. Off the landing there are two further double bedrooms, bathroom and separate WC. The renovation works included heavy insulation to the walls and ceiling, bespoke wooden double glazed windows (by the Green Building Store) and a wet underfloor heating system to the ground floor. It is connected to mains electricity and has an lpg gas supply – the tank is located opposite by the farm building. It is connected to a spring water supply shared with 4 other properties and drainage is to its own private sewage treatment plan. To the rear of the house there is an attractively landscaped garden area with ornamental pond and a further lawned garden beyond. Available as an additional extra by separate negotiation, there are over 12 acres of additional grazing land, ideal for equestrian use, grazing and mowing. This includes a detached workshop / forge. Also available by separate negotiation is a modern steel framed blockwork building which incorporates stables, a studio space with kitchenette, shower and outside wc and the central heating boiler and water purification system. Ground floor open plan living space 31\' 5" x 27\' 5 overall" (9.58m x 8.36m) The property is entered through a glass door to the front which gives access into this large open plan living space. It is open to two storeys in height with the original aisled timber frame on display set upon stone batts. It has a polished concrete floor with underfloor heating, 2 full height windows to the front and 2 further full height windows and a door to the rear. There is a slightly raised sitting area with fireplace, log burning stove and a further window to the side. A cantilevered wooden staircase with glazed balustrade leads up to the first floor. Storage cupboard A full sized walk in storage cupboard recessed off the living space. Downstairs WC / shower 7\' 9" x 3\' 1" (2.36m x 0.94m) With modern three piece suite comprising low flush wc, hand washbasin and shower cubicle, tiled walls and extractor. First floor landing Featuring a low exposed roof truss and steps down into bedroom 2. Bedroom 2 12\' 6" x 9\' 2" (3.81m x 2.79m) A double bedroom with windows to the rear, rooflight to the angled ceiling, part exposed roof truss and central heating radiator. Bedroom 3 12\' 5" x 10\' (3.78m x 3.05m) Featuring exposed roof truss and rooflight to the angled ceiling, recessed eaves storage area and central heating radiator. Bathroom 7\' 5" x 7\' 4 (3\'5" min)" (2.26m x 2.24m) With pedestal washbasin and bath with shower over, rooflight and exposed beam to the angled ceiling, tiled walls tiled floor and central heating radiator. Continue along this lane which leads through the woods and down to Scout Hall and cluster of other smaller buildings. The Aisled Barn will be found at the foot of this lane.'

Rooms First Floor Principal Bedroom (3.37 x 3.01 m) En-Suite (1.01 x 2.78 m) Bedroom 2 (2.56 x 3.46 m) Bedroom 3 (2.02 x 3.46 m) Bathroom (1.7 x 1.96 m) Ground Floor Lounge (4.68 x 3.91 m) Kitchen (2.91 x 3.45 m) Dining (1.76 x 2.4 m) WC (1.67 x .96 m) About The Woods At City Fields Perfectly situated for the amenities and attractions of Wakefield, The Woods, which forms part of the wider City Fields neighbourhood, has easy access to the M1 and M62 and is well within commuting range of Leeds. There are bus services into the city centre and Wakefield benefits from good rail links. Of the two railway stations, Westgate is on the Leeds to London route, with journey times of less than 15 minutes to Leeds and two hours to London Kings Cross, while Kirkgate serves stations to Sheffield and Nottingham. The city of Wakefield presents a superb choice of cultural and leisure attractions set against a background of fascinating architecture and heritage, including the magnificent Wakefield Cathedral and Sandal Castle. In addition to visual arts at The Hepworth, Yorkshire Sculpture Park and several smaller galleries, the Theatre Royal presents an eclectic programme of drama and music, and the new Unity Works is a vibrant venue for social gatherings and live music. There is an excellent choice of cinemas, bars, restaurants and nightlife, including soul nights at the celebrated Red Bar. Wakefield’s sporting and leisure provision include the superb Pugneys Watersports Centre and Country Park on the southern edge of the city, where there are facilities for sailing, windsurfing and canoeing, and the choice of leisure centres in the area includes Sun Lane Leisure, where there is a 25m swimming pool, a fitness suite and a gym. Other amenities nearby include Normanton Golf Club, around a mile to the north, and Pontefract Racecourse is less than ten miles away. The City Fields proposals include a neighbourhood centre within a short walk of the homes, with a range of shops including food retailers, restaurants, a medical centre and other services. There is also a small local shopping area on Windhill Road with a pharmacist, a post office and a convenience store, while the city centre offers a very wide choice of high street chains, malls and traditional shops. A major recycling centre on Denby Dale Road, three and a half miles away, accepts virtually all household packaging, electrical items and clothing. An area within the wider City Fields neighbourhood, close to Wakefield City Academy, has been set aside for educational provision. However, there is also a choice of established primary schools within walking distance, from where pupils normally move on to either Outwood Grange Academy or St Thomas à Becket rc College for secondary education. There is a large fulltime gp practice at New Southgate Surgery, approximately a mile and a half away, and Pinderfields General Hospital, around half a mile from The Woods, operates a round-the- clock A&E department. Opening Hours Pop in to visit us anytime during our opening hours and find out how we could help you move here; no appointment is needed. If you would prefer to, you can still make an appointment by calling our sales centre or booking on our website. Disclaimer The house plans shown above, including the room specifications, may vary from development to development and are provided for general guidance only. For more accurate and detailed plans for a specific plot, please check with your local Miller Homes sales adviser. Carpets and floor coverings are not included in our homes as standard.'

text_description: Tucked away at the top of the street, in a quiet cul de sac with a rural feel and amazing woodland views, you could almost be in the countryside - but a short walk takes you to Roundhay Park and Oakwood Parade. Although appearing modest from the front, this is a lovely, large split level property, set well back from the road, with a pretty front garden. On entering from the driveway, you come into the top floor of the house. A porch and spacious double height hallway welcomes you. To the right is a snug family room, perfect for curling up on a winter's evening. To the left is the beautiful modern kitchen, with plenty of space for a dining table. With high quality fittings and appliances, you'll love cooking and entertaining here. It has plenty of room for its large cooker with a 5 ring induction hob, double oven and separate grill. There's also an integrated microwave and dishwasher, as well as lots of larder cupboards and storage. The adjacent utility room has fitted cupboards and space for a big fridge freezer and is plumbed for a washing machine. We now come to two of the highlights of this home: A huge dining room, with polished wooden flooring and sliding glass doors to a balcony, and a large living room. Both have floor to ceiling windows connecting the house with the wonderful woodland views: Spectacular! An external door from the living room leads to a wooden balcony, ideal for sitting out on a summer evening, or to wander down the outside stairway for a stroll round the gardens. There is also a very generously sized double bedroom on this floor, with built-in wardrobes and a modern ensuite. Finally, there is a guest WC with handbasin just off the hallway. Moving downstairs, there is a cloakroom in the hallway and 3 further double bedrooms. All have built-in wardrobes or cupboards, with the smallest having direct access to the covered patio, below the family room. There is also a dressing room with built-in wardrobes leading to the clean, bright and modern family bathroom. It's a great size, with a spa bath and plenty of room for its freestanding shower, toilet and sink. For a real touch of luxury and relaxation, you also have a wood-lined sauna linked to it! At the front of the house is a wide driveway for easy parking of at least two cars, as well as a large garage with an electric door. The garage also has a water and electricity supply, and access at the back via a wooden stairway. The front garden leads you down to the main entrance and gives the house further privacy. At the back is an amazing garden. It has a long lawn, beautiful mature shrubs, bushes and trees, with paths and steps winding round the distinctive landscaped areas. A backdrop of mature trees gives wonderful privacy and helps make this a very special place indeed. Over the course of the last 10 years, the house has undergone a gradual programme of improvements and modernisation, with a rebuilt and extended living room, replacement boiler, new bathrooms, new kitchen and utility room, redecorating and skimming of artex ceilings, timber flooring in the dining room as well as new carpeting. It also has planning permission granted for enclosing the lower ground floor patio area to provide an additional large living area looking onto the garden. Finally, the location is hard to beat. As well as nearby Roundhay Park and Oakwood Parade, it is close to Roundhay School - both the primary and secondary campuses, as well as Roundhay St John primary and a Montessori nursery. Regular buses run along Wetherby road, at the bottom of the street, and the ring road is easily accessible. Additional Information: Council Tax: Band F Please take time to study our 2D and 3D floor plans and browse our photographs. This house is sure to gain a lot of interest so please contact EweMove North Leeds 24/7 by telephone or online to book a viewing on our HomeLaunch day, Sunday 18th December. text_description: 'Offered with no onward chain a well presented, three bedroom, mid townhouse with spacious dining kitchen, driveway parking and integral garage. An inner hallway leads to the spacious dining kitchen to the rear, a great entertaining room with ample room for a good sized dining table and with fabulous long distance views. Ilkley boasts an excellent wide range of high-class shops, restaurants, cafés, pubs and everyday amenities including two supermarkets, health centre, library and Playhouse theatre and boutique cinema. Ilkley is an ideal town for the commuter with frequent train services to Leeds and Bradford (around 35 minutes’ commute), providing regular connections to London Kings Cross. Leeds Bradford International Airport is just over 11 miles away with national and international services. There are bus services into the city centre and Wakefield benefits from good rail links. Of the two railway stations, Westgate is on the Leeds to London route, with journey times of less than 15 minutes to Leeds and two hours to London Kings Cross, while Kirkgate serves stations to Sheffield and Nottingham. The city of Wakefield presents a superb choice of cultural and leisure attractions set against a background of fascinating architecture and heritage, including the magnificent Wakefield Cathedral and Sandal Castle. In addition to visual arts at The Hepworth, Yorkshire Sculpture Park and several smaller galleries, the Theatre Royal presents an eclectic programme of drama and music, and the new Unity Works is a vibrant venue for social gatherings and live music. There is an excellent choice of cinemas, bars, restaurants and nightlife, including soul nights at the celebrated Red Bar. Wakefield’s sporting and leisure provision include the superb Pugneys Watersports Centre and Country Park on the southern edge of the city, where there are facilities for sailing, windsurfing and canoeing, and the choice of leisure centres in the area includes Sun Lane Leisure, where there is a 25m swimming pool, a fitness suite and a gym. Other amenities nearby include Normanton Golf Club, around a mile to the north, and Pontefract Racecourse is less than ten miles away. The City Fields proposals include a neighbourhood centre within a short walk of the homes, with a range of shops including food retailers, restaurants, a medical centre and other services. There is also a small local shopping area on Windhill Road with a pharmacist, a post office and a convenience store, while the city centre offers a very wide choice of high street chains, malls and traditional shops. A major recycling centre on Denby Dale Road, three and a half miles away, accepts virtually all household packaging, electrical items and clothing. An area within the wider City Fields neighbourhood, close to Wakefield City Academy, has been set aside for educational provision. However, there is also a choice of established primary schools within walking distance, from where pupils normally move on to either Outwood Grange Academy or St Thomas à Becket rc College for secondary education. There is a large fulltime gp practice at New Southgate Surgery, approximately a mile and a half away, and Pinderfields General Hospital, around half a mile from The Woods, operates a round-the- clock A&E department.
